articles.title: Asian Para Games: Prachi Yadav continues to shine, clinches gold in Canoe women's KL2 event
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: India's Prachi Yadav won a gold medal in the Canoe women's KL2 event at the 4th Asian Para Games, adding to her impressive performance. Yadav had alre
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's Prachi Yadav continued her impressive performance in the 4th Asian Para Games by clinching a gold medal in the Canoe women's KL2 event. Prachi's victory added to the flurry of medals that India has been winning in the ongoing event.Prachi had already secured a silver medal on Day 1 in the women's VL2 final, narrowly missing out on the gold. In the women's KL2 event, she finished on top with a timing of 54.962 seconds. China's Shanshan Wang claimed the silver medal with a timing of 55.674 seconds, while Iran's Roya Soltani settled for the bronze with a timing of 56.714 seconds.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) On the first day of competition, Prachi had a close battle with Uzbekistan's Irodakhon Rustamova. Both athletes were separated by a mere 1.022 seconds, with Prachi securing a silver medal with a timing of 1:03.47 seconds, while Irodakhon claimed the gold with a timing of 1:02.125 seconds. Japan's Saki Komatsu won the bronze medal with a timing of 1:11.635 seconds.In the Canoe Men's KL3 Final event, Manish Kaurav secured a bronze medal with a timing of 44.605 seconds. He narrowly missed the gold, falling short by just 2.347 seconds. Uzbekistan's Khasan Kuldashev won the gold medal with a timing of 42.258 seconds, and Kazakhstan's Zhalgas Taikenov claimed the silver with a timing of 44.605 seconds.Simran Vats delivered a stunning performance, securing a silver medal in the women's 100m T12 event during Tuesday's action at the ongoing 4th Asian Para Games. She clocked an impressive 12.68 seconds, coming oh-so-close to the gold, missing it by a mere 0.16 seconds.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) The gold went to Indonesia's Ni Made Arianti Putri, who not only claimed the top spot but also set a new Asian Para Games record with a remarkable time of 12.52 seconds. This feat surpassed the previous record held by China's Guohua Zhou, who had maintained it for nine years with a timing of 12.56 seconds.With Prachi's gold, Simran's silver and Manish's bronze, India's medal count at the 4th Asian Para Games continued to grow, building on the success of Day 1. The Indian contingent, which includes 303 athletes, has high hopes for further medal victories in the competition.In the 2018 Asian Para Games, India sent 190 athletes and secured 72 medals, including 15 gold, marking their best performance at the event at that time.(With ANI inputs)

articles.title: Deepthi Jeevanji sets new Asian Para Games record with gold in 400m-T20
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: India's Deepthi Jeevanji won a gold medal in the women's 400m-T20 event at the 4th Asian Para Games, setting a new Asian Para Games record with a time
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India continues to shine in the 4th Asian Para Games, with Deepthi Jeevanji securing a gold medal in the women's 400m-T20 event. Deepthi set a new Asian Para Games record and games record with her exceptional time of 56.69 seconds. This remarkable performance earned her the top spot on the podium.Thailand's Orawan Kaising gave her best effort, clocking a personal best of 59.00 seconds, but she had to settle for the silver medal. Japan's Niina Kanno won the bronze with a personal best time of 59.73 seconds.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) In the men's 400m-T64 final, Ajay Kumar secured a silver medal with a personal best time of 54.85 seconds. However, Saudi Arabia's Nour Mohammed set a new Asian Para record with a remarkable time of 52.81 seconds, earning him the gold medal. Thailand's Jafa Seapla secured the bronze with a time of 55.09 seconds.Earlier on the same day, Manish Kaurav won a bronze medal in the Canoe Men's KL3 Final event, marking India's medal count on Day 2 of the competition. Manish recorded a time of 44.605 seconds, narrowly missing the gold by just 2.347 seconds. Uzbekistan's Khasan Kuldashev clinched the gold with a time of 42.258 seconds, and Kazakhstan's Zhalgas Taikenov secured the silver with a time of 44.605 seconds.With these impressive performances, India aims to maintain its successful streak, building on the 17 medals (6 gold, 6 silver, and 5 bronze) achieved on Day 1. The Indian contingent, comprising 303 athletes (191 men and 112 women), is the largest group participating in the fourth edition of the Asian Para Games.In the 2018 Asian Para Games, India sent 190 athletes and achieved its best-ever performance, winning 72 medals, including 15 gold medals. The Indian athletes are determined to continue their strong showing in this year's competition.(With ANI inputs)

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Ekta Bhyan clinches bronze in women's Club Throw - F32/51 event
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: India continued its impressive performance at the 4th Asian Para Games, winning more medals on Day 2. Ekta Bhyan won a bronze in the women's Club Thro
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India continued to shine at the 4th Asian Para Games, securing more medals on Day 2 of the competition. In the women's Club Throw - F32/51 event, Ekta Bhyan won a bronze medal. Ekta, who was the previous Asian Para Games record-holder, faced a tough challenge from Iran's Parastoo Habibi, who broke the record with an attempt of 22.88m in her first throw. Although Ekta responded with a brilliant throw of 21.66m, she couldn't reclaim the record and had to settle for bronze. Parastoo secured the gold medal, and UAE's Thekra Ahmed Saeed claimed silver.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) In the men's 400m-T64 final, Ajay Kumar gave an exceptional performance with a personal best timing of 54.85s, earning him a silver medal. Saudi Arabia's Nour Mohammed set a new Asian Para Games record with a timing of 52.81s to win gold, while Thailand's Jafa Seapla took home the bronze with a timing of 55.09s.In canoeing, Gajendra Singh won a bronze medal in the Men's VL2 final with a timing of 1:01.084s. The gold medal went to Iran's Islam Jahedi with a timing of 55.749s, and Thailand's Santi Wantawee secured the silver.The Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games, consisting of 303 athletes, continued to excel, aiming to replicate the success of Day 1, where they ended with a total of 17 medals – 6 gold, 6 silver, and 5 bronze. The athletes' remarkable performances have showcased their dedication and skill on the international stage. India's participation in the games has been the largest contingent ever sent to the Asian Para Games, emphasizing the country's commitment to promoting para sports.In the 2018 Asian Para Games, India sent 190 athletes and achieved a significant breakthrough, returning with a total of 72 medals, including 15 gold medals. The current performance suggests that Indian para athletes are determined to surpass their previous success and continue making their mark in the world of para sports.(With ANI inputs)

articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: Indian para-athletes Sumit Antil and Pushpendra Singh won gold and bronze medals in the men's Javelin Throw-F64 final at the 4th Asian Para Games. Ant
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Indian para-athletes Sumit Antil and Pushpendra Singh made their nation proud by achieving gold and bronze medals in the men's Javelin Throw-F64 final on Day 3 of the 4th Asian Para Games. Sumit Antil's outstanding performance earned him the gold medal while setting new records in the event. He broke the Asian Para Games record, the World record, and the Asian record with a phenomenal throw of 73.29 meters, accomplished during his third attempt of the competition.Asian Para Games: Day 3The silver medal in the event went to Sri Lanka's Arachchige Samitha, who recorded a throw of 62.42 meters. Sumit's compatriot, Pushpendra Singh, secured the bronze medal with a throw of 62.06 meters. The Indian para-athletes' exceptional performances have resulted in a successful campaign for India at the 4th Asian Para Games.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) With these remarkable achievements, India currently holds the fifth position in the medal standings, having won a total of 36 medals, including 10 gold, 12 silver, and 14 bronze medals. The Indian contingent at the 4th Asian Para Games consists of 303 athletes, including 191 men and 112 women, marking the largest participation in the history of the continental event.This year's performance builds on India's success at the 2018 Asian Para Games, where the nation sent 190 athletes and returned with an impressive tally of 72 medals, including 15 gold. The achievements of Sumit Antil and Pushpendra Singh represent the nation's commitment to para-athletics and its dedication to excelling on the international stage.(With ANI inputs)

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil breaks world record, leads India's 30-medal haul on Day 3
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: India's medal tally reached 64 (15 gold, 20 silver, 29 bronze), with this being the most successful day, where 17 of the 30 medals, including all six
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's reigning Paralympic champion, Sumit Antil, broke his own javelin throw F64 world record with an astonishing 73.29m effort, securing the gold medal on the third day of the Hangzhou Asian Para Games on Wednesday. India's medal tally reached 64 (15 gold, 20 silver, 29 bronze), with this being the most successful day, where 17 of the 30 medals, including all six golds, came from athletics.Antil, aged 25, exceeded his previous world record of 70.83m. He was joined on the podium by another Indian, Pushpendra Singh, who claimed the bronze with a 62.06m throw. Antil, who hails from Sonepat, achieved this remarkable feat in the F64 category for athletes with a leg amputation, competing with prosthetics in a standing position.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Additionally, Ankur Dhama made history as the first Indian to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games, taking the top spot in the men's T11 1500m race with a time of 4:27.70, having also won gold in the men's T11 5000m race the previous day. — Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Sundar Singh Gurjar set a new world record in the men's F46 javelin throw with a distance of 68.60m, surpassing the previous record of 67.79m. Indian athletes swept all three medals in the men's F46 javelin throw event, with Rinku and Ajeet Singh taking silver and bronze, respectively. — Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) The women's T11 1500m event saw India clinch the gold and silver medals with Rakshitha Raju and Killaka Lalitha taking the top two positions.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Haney and Nimisha Suresh Chakkungalparambil added gold medals in the men's F37/38 javelin throw and women's T47 long jump events. — Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Additionally, India secured a silver in women's F54/55 discus throw and bronze medals in men's T35 200m and T37 200m.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) In para table tennis, Bhavina Patel won a bronze in women's singles Class 4, and Sandeep Dangi secured another bronze in men's singles class 1. In para archery, India won two silver medals and a bronze. In para badminton, India clinched six bronze medals, while in para powerlifting, Zainab Khatun and Rajkumari won a silver and a bronze, respectively, in the women's 61kg category.(With PTI inputs)

articles.title: India creates history in Asian Para Games, takes tally to record 82 medals
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: Indian para athletes on Thursday created history by winning the highest number of medals in the Asian Para Games, taking the country's tally to 82, in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian para athletes on Thursday achieved a historic milestone, securing the highest number of medals in the Asian Para Games in Hangzhou and raised the country's tally to a whopping 82, including an impressive 18 gold medals. The remarkable accomplishment surpasses India's previous record of 72 medals achieved during the 2018 edition held in Indonesia. On the fourth day, India clinched 18 medals, including three golds.India's medals tally stood at 18 gold, 23 silver and 41 bronze at the end of Day 4 of the competitions.India's position in the medals tally, however, dropped two places to eight, as not too many gold medals were won on Thursday.South Korea and Indonesia moved ahead of India in the medals tally led by China (156 gold, 128 silver, 108 bronze).With two more days left in the Games, the country is on course of achieving its target of 100 medals in this edition of the Games.India had won 72 medals (15 gold, 24 silver, 33 bronze) in the last edition in Jakarta which was the best before the Hangzhou Games.Eight medals, including one gold, were won by track and field athletes on Thursday.Overall, athletics contributed 45 medals out of India's total of 82, and 14 gold out of the country's total of 18 so far.Sachin Sarjerao Khilari won the first gold of the day in men's F46 shot put with a Games record throw of 16.03m while Rohit Kumar took the bronze with 14.56m.Para shooter Sidhartha Babu then bagged another gold in R6 mixed 50m rifle prone SH1 event as he shot an Asian Para Games score of 247.7.The compound mixed team of Sheetal Devi and Rakesh Kumar won a gold after defeating their Chinese counterparts Lin Yueshan and Ai Xinliang 151-149 in the final.India also won a bronze medal in archery men's doubles W1 event with the pair of Adil Mohamed Nazir Ansari and Naveen Dalal defeating the Kazakh pair of Nurshat Toleukassym and Sagdat Duisembayev 125-120.Simran and Bhagyashri Madhavrao Jadhav won a silver each in women's T12 100m and women's F34 shot put respectively. Simran clocked 26.12 seconds while Jadhav cleared 7.54m.Monu Ghangas also picked up a silver in men's F11 discus throw with an effort of 37.87m.Narayan Thakur won a bronze in men's T35 100m with a time of 14.37 seconds. Shreyansh Trivedi also took a bronze in men's T37 100m with a time of 12.24 seconds. Muthuraja also won a bronze in the men's F55 shot put with a throw of 10.42m.In para badminton, Sukant Indukant Kadam (men's singles SL4), Sivan Nithya Sumathy (women's singles SH6), Manisha Ramadass (women's singles SU5), Mandeep Kaur/Manisha Ramadass (women's doubles SL3-SU5), Krishna Nagar/Sivarajan Solaimalai (men's doubles SH6) and Pramod Bhagat/Sukant Indukant Kadam (men's doubles SL3-SL4) won a bronze medal each after losing their respective semifinal matches.In chess, Bhaveshkumar Rathi Himanshi picked up a bronze in women's individual standard VI-B1 event.(With inputs from PTI)

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Armless archer Sheetal becomes first Indian woman to win two gold in single edition, country's tally touches record 99
articles.summary: Asian Games 2023 News: Teenage armless archer Sheetal Devi achieved a historic feat by becoming the first Indian woman to secure two gold medals in a single edition of the A
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Teenage armless archer Sheetal Devi achieved a historic feat by becoming the first Indian woman to secure two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games. India's record-breaking performance reached a total of 99 medals on the penultimate day of the competitions in Hangzhou.India amassed an impressive 17 medals, including seven gold On Friday with the shuttlers making the most significant contribution, clinching eight medals, including four gold.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) As the Hangzhou Asian Para Games entered its final day, India stood at the sixth position in the overall standings, boasting 25 gold, 29 silver, and 45 bronze medals. The top positions were held by China (196 gold, 159 silver, 138 bronze), Japan (39, 44, 56), Iran (39, 39, 37), Korea (28, 30, 37), and Indonesia (26, 21, 32).— 19thAGofficial (@19thAGofficial) In terms of the total number of medals, India held the fourth position. The nation had already surpassed its previous highest Asian Para Games medal tally of 72 medals (15 gold, 24 silver, 33 bronze) achieved during the 2018 edition.India is now on the cusp of achieving a remarkable milestone by securing 100 medals in the Hangzhou Asian Para Games.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) The para athletes are set to emulate their able-bodied counterparts who had won a record haul of 107 medals in the Hangzhou Asian Games held from September 23 to October 8.Sheetal clinched the women's individual compound gold on Friday to add to the yellow metal she won in the compound mixed team event on Thursday.In fact, it is a hat-trick of medals for the 16-year-old from Jammu and Kashmir, who holds her bow with her foot. She had also won a silver in the women's doubles compound event.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Sheetal was born with phocomelia syndrome, a rare congenital disorder which kept limbs underdeveloped.Discovered at a military camp in a remote part of Kishtwar and adopted by the Indian Army in her childhood, Sheetal, who became the first armless woman to win a Para World Archery Championships medal in July, defeated Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah 144-142 in the gold medal match.Ankur Dhama had become the first Indian to win two gold medals in a single edition earlier this week.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) Another Indian archer, Rakesh Kumar defeated Iran's Alisin Manshaezadeh in 144(10)-144(9) in a shoot-off to win the silver medal in men's compound event.Reigning Paralympic champion shuttler Pramod Bhagat secured a gold medal in the single SL3 category as he outplayed compatriot Nitesh Kumar 22-20, 21-19 in the final."Firstly a huge congratulations to Nitesh Kumar, I think he played the game of his life, but unfortunately ended up with a silver. He is a brilliant player and pushes me till the edge which he did today," said Bhagat.— Media_SAI (@Media_SAI) "Somehow even when I was trailing, I had a belief that I would make a comeback and could win, the thought of losing never occurred to me. I focused on 1 point at a time and made it possible," he added.Tokyo Paralympics silver medallist IAS officer Suhas Lalinakere Yathiraj bettered his bronze from the last edition by winning gold in the SL4 final.Thulasimathi Murugesan warded off the challenge posed by local shuttler Yang Qiuxia by eking out a 21-19, 21-19 win to clinch the coveted yellow metal in the women's SU5 final.In the men's doubles SL3-SLF4, Nitesh and Tarun won the gold, while Thulasmathi combined with Manasi Joshi to win silver in women's doubles SL3-SU5, losing to Khalimatus Sadiyah and Leani Ratri Oktila of Indonesia 16-21, 21-13, 14-21 in the final.Reigning Paralympic champion Krishna Nagar settled for a silver as he went down fighting 10 -21, 21-8, 11-21 against Hong Kong's Chu Man Kai in the men's SH6 final.The Indian men's SU5 men's doubles pair of Chirag Baretha and Raj Kumar also added a silver after losing to Hafizh Briliansyah and Dheva Anrimusthi of Indonesia 11-21, 21-19, 11-21 in the final.Badminton competitions ended on Friday and the shuttlers contributed 21 medals (4 gold, 4 silver, 13 bronze) to India's tally, the second highest after athletics -- which has contributed 51 so far.In athletics, which contributed six medals on Friday, Raman Sharma and Dharamraj Solairaj picked up a gold medal each in men's 1500m T38 and long jump T64 events.Raman reigned supreme in his event with a new Asian and Games record time of 4:20.80s, while Dharamraj also broke the same two records by clearing a distance of 6.80m.Javelin throwers Pradeep Kumar (25.94m) and Laxit (21.20m) clinched the silver and bronze medals in the F54 event with personal best efforts.Discus thrower Lakshmi too found a place on the podium as she bagged the bronze medal with a personal best effort of 22.55m in the women's F37.38. Manu also won a bronze medal in the men's shot put F37 event with a personal best effort of 14.09m.Suyash Narayan Jadhav won India's first medal in swimming in Hangzhou as he picked up a bronze in men's 50m butterfly S7, clocking 32.22 seconds.(With PTI Inputs)

articles.title: Herd Hierarchy: Are The Bills The NFL's Best Team, Or Do Seahawks Remain No. 1?
articles.summary: Colin Cowherd revealed his Herd Hierarchy rankings heading into Week 3.
articles.body: The Los Angeles Rams are back, and quarterback injuries were just a couple of the storylines from an interesting Week 2 of the NFL. Colin Cowherd revealed his Herd Hierarchy rankings, which featured a new team at No. 1 and five new teams in the rankings after their dominant wins last weekend. Here are Cowherd's Week 2 Herd Hierarchy rankings: 10. Detroit LionsRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: Unranked Cowherd’s thoughts: I’m going to put the Lions at 10 because of their firepower. They’ve scored 30-plus in both games and allowed 30-plus in both games. Outside of Aidan Hutchinson, not sure who else I trust on the defensive side. But Jared Goff is the only quarterback this season with six touchdowns and no picks. They rank second offensively in big plays, but last in big plays allowed. I like the GM, I like the coach, I like the offensive firepower. Once again, it feels like an annual thing; they’re banged up defensively. I don’t trust them holding leads. But it’s an offensive league; they’ve got a ton of firepower. 9. New Orleans SaintsRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: Unranked Cowherd's thoughts: Is anybody paying attention to the Saints? They outscored the Ravens in Baltimore 15-0 in the fourth. Tyler Shough, they found their guy. He’s sneaky athletic. He’s got size. He’s throwing the ball to the right guy, Chris Olave. In the fourth quarter in overtime this year, two road games, 78% completion. They have a real roster. We picked them to win their division. They looked very good in the second half of both Detroit and Baltimore. They dominated the Ravens like people don’t do in Baltimore. 8. New England PatriotsRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: Unranked Cowherd's thoughts: Drake Maye’s been uneven. A.J. Brown is unavailable. But I’ll put the Patriots, who are 14-2 in their last 16 games. They win, and when Christian Gonzalez is healthy, it is an excellent defense. They’re one of seven teams to allow 300 or fewer yards in the first two weeks. They held the Steelers to three and a half yards per play. I still think their O-line is mid. We’ll keep our fingers crossed on how A.J. Brown works, but coaching, culture, defensive front, elite secondary — I got the Patriots at eight. 7. Los Angeles RamsRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: Unranked Cowherd's thoughts: We all know the Rams are better than seven, but they don’t have Myles Garrett; they don’t have Puka Nacua. They’re not, I don’t think, dialed in yet. [Matthew] Stafford got lucky a few times last night. Davante Adams made some insane catches, but it’s a little Noah’s Ark. Three tight ends I like, two defensive interior linemen, a couple of rush edges, two good running backs. Stafford is not going to give you a lot of wiggle. They’re, right now, not entirely polished, not playing clean football. There’s fumbles. There’s interceptions. There’s penalties. They’re better than seven, but that’s where I’ll put them now. 6. Philadelphia EaglesRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: 10 ↑ Cowherd's thoughts: I’ll say the same about the Eagles; they’re in a three-and-out factory. In September the last five years, they’re 14-2. Nobody wins ugly like Philadelphia. I will say, [Dontayvion] Wicks and DeVonta Smith are a real tandem. Makai Lemon hasn’t done anything as a rookie wide receiver; they haven’t needed him. The offense isn’t clicking. They’re 14th in scoring, 14th in yards per play. I can like Jalen Hurts simultaneously and think sometimes he holds them back." 5. Cincinnati BengalsRecord: 1-1Previous ranking: 9 ↑ Cowherd's thoughts: Keep your eye on Cincinnati. The Bengals spent money on defense. It was the worst run defense in the league. All I'm going to say is, it's not anymore. They look different. They are forcing turnovers. They have a very physical defensive front. They didn't even play well against the Texans, and dominated them. They held the running backs to 18 rush yards on 14 carries. They have solved a big dilemma. I think they were going to be viewed as one of the most improved teams in the NFL, and so far, they are. 4. Kansas City ChiefsRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 7 ↑ Cowherd's thoughts: They don't have Josh Simmons; that does worry me. But have you noticed that Travis Kelce looks 26 years old? It's amazing when you have a legitimate running game, you can't cheat against Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice. Suddenly, Rice looks like a great deep threat. And Travis Kelce is wide open. And that's what happens when you have a run game and safeties can't cheat and linebackers can't cheat. [Patrick] Mahomes looks spry. If you look at yards per play allowed, it's Andy's best defense. Is it? I don't know. But they're only allowing four and a half yards per play. 3. San Francisco 49ersRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 6 ↑ Cowherd's thoughts: It's hard to judge the Niners. All the old guys are healthy, and Miami's going to help everyone's data look great. But Brock Purdy, playing with leads, and he's barely been hit, and he hasn't been sacked. So it's kind of hard to say. It's like a dominant college team; Brock Purdy hasn't even been rushed. But I will say this: they've had 11 incomplete passes and 10 scoring drives. So they're accomplishing what they should. And we know when healthy: [Christian] McCaffrey, [George] Kittle, Trent [Williams], Fred Warner, these are all Hall of Famers, and [Nick] Bosa. We know their top end's great. But the question is, will they be available on Thanksgiving? 2. Buffalo BillsRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 1 ↓ Cowherd's thoughts: Offensive coach with Josh Allen has really been pivotal. Dalton Kincaid leads all tight ends in receiving yards. The defense looks good enough; they've spent a lot of draft capital on this defense. But I think Josh Allen, I think most quarterbacks are all better with an offensive head coach. Doesn't mean you can't win Super Bowls, like Seattle with a defensive head coach. They're facing the Los Angeles Chargers this week; good luck to Los Angeles there. 1. Seattle SeahawksRecord: 2-0Previous ranking: 2 ↑ Cowherd's thoughts: Only Seattle can go to a backup [quarterback] — a backup most of us don't love — and throttle teams. I don't know what their weakness is. They're even good on special teams. They lose a running back, but they still have a great run game. They lose a top corner, two of them, and still have good corners. [Jaxon Smith-Njigba] is 40% of their offense; you worry a little about that. They're very JSN-dependent. He has four of their five total touchdowns this year. But [Sam] Darnold gives them an athletic lingo they don't currently have with Drew Lock. They're allowing 3.8 yards per play. They are the fastest defense, to me, sideline to sideline in the NFL. articles.title: Mahomes Mountain Week 3: Josh Allen Takes Over The Top Spot
articles.summary: Nick Wright's quarterback mountain has a new occupant at the top.
articles.body: Nick Wright's quarterback mountain has a new occupant at the top. Trevor Lawrence's stay at No. 1 lasted exactly one week, and after a Sunday that included a bad half from Lamar Jackson, a big statistical outing that still wasn't enough for Patrick Mahomes to take the top spot. The injury list keeps growing, too. Sam Darnold, Jayden Daniels and Jaxson Dart are all off the mountain due to injuries. So who does that leave at the top? Here's how Wright sees the league's quarterbacks entering Week 3: Off The Mountain: Aaron RodgersPittsburgh Steelers Jameis WinstonNew York Giants Cam WardTennessee Titans Malik WillisMiami Dolphins Jayden DanielsWashington Commanders Jaxson DartNew York Giants Sam DarnoldSeattle Seahawks Wright: "Sadly, we must start with off the mountain, and the growing list of quarterback injuries. Take a moment, pour one out for 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers. I don't know if he gets back on the mountain. I don't know how interested he is in climbing the mountain, and I'm sure it's all Mike McCarthy's fault." "Jameis Winston is going to be pressed into service. Cam Ward almost got the best win of his career. Malik Willis is in a tough spot." On the injury list, Wright said: "Jayden Daniels evidently might not want to have surgery. Jaxson Dart, we're still awaiting the news on. Darnold could be back soon, but he's been out, so he's off the mountain." articles.title: Pranati Nayak qualifies for Asian Games vault final, sets up shot at redemption
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: After a disappointing show at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Pranati Nayak gave herself a chance to make amends by qualifying for the vault final .
articles.body: After a disappointing show at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, Pranati Nayak gave herself a chance to make amends by qualifying for the vault final at the Asian Games on Tuesday.The 31-year-old, India’s lone artistic gymnast at the continental meet, finished seventh in the qualification round at Nagoya General Gymnasium with an aggregate score of 12.916 that also included a bonus of 0.20.In her first vault — a Tsukahara back 360-degree turn with straight body — which had a difficulty value of 4.4, Pranati earned 8.600 for execution to score 13.000. She followed it up with a 4.0-difficulty vault — handspring pike forward somersault with half turn — scoring 8.433 for execution earning a total of 12.433.It was enough to scrape through to the final, which will also feature Uzbekistan’s 51-year-old Oksana Chusovitina after she qualified in fourth spot with an aggregate score of 13.266.The two-time Olympic medallist, who missed the 2006 and 2010 Asian Games while representing Germany, is competing in her seventh edition of the continental meet. When Chusovitina made her Asian Games debut in Hiroshima in 1994, several members of the 2026 field were not yet born.For Pranati’s coach Ashok Mishra, however, the result was significant for a simpler reason: she had achieved the target he had set before the competition.“It’s going to be a very difficult test for her. But I think she will do well,” Mishra had told TOI before the Games.Considering she was struggling with plantar fasciitis, much of Pranati's recent training had also been about getting comfortable with the physical and psychological demands of the landing, with Mishra using soft-landing equipment and the foam pit before shifting her to the main landing area.Pranati, however, showed no signs of discomfort on Tuesday as she secured place in the final, although there was little separating her from the gymnasts immediately below her.As for South Korea’s Seojeong Yeo, she led the field with a score of 14.466 to qualify comfortably for the final. North Korea’s Chang Ok An was second on 13.900, while China’s DU Siyu secured the third qualifying spot with 13.433.For Pranati, who trains at Odisha AM/NS India Gymnastics High-Performance Centre in Bhubaneswar, the qualification provides an opportunity to put behind the disappointment of Glasgow, where a lack of speed in her approach disrupted her first vault and kept her out of the final.She will now return to the runway on Thursday with the chance to improve on Tuesday’s performance when the medals are decided.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: World body threatens suspension of equestrian federation over failure to hold elections
articles.summary: More sports News: New Delhi: The Fédération Equestre Internationale (FEI), the global governing body for equestrian sport, has threatened to suspend the Equestrian Fede.
articles.body: New Delhi: The Fédération Equestre Internationale (FEI), the global governing body for equestrian sport, has threatened to suspend the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), citing governance concerns and failure to complete the electoral process within the timeline set by the Delhi High Court.TOI is in possession of the FEI mail sent to the EFI, in which the international body has sought a written explanation by Sept 28. The matter is expected to go before the FEI Board on Oct 13 for possible suspension.The FEI has questioned whether the present arrangement provides for a governing body elected by members under a constitution compliant with India’s applicable sports law, including the National Sports Governance Act.The letter points to the ad-hoc committee constituted by the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) on March 27 to administer the EFI. The Delhi High Court had directed the committee to finalise the federation’s constitution and by-laws within two months and notify elections within the subsequent 30 days.According to the FEI, the stipulated period ended on June 27 without a revised constitution being communicated as approved and without fresh elections being conducted.The FEI has invoked Article 8.3 of its Statutes, under which its Board can suspend a national federation for breaching principles laid down in Article 2, after giving it an opportunity to be heard. The letter specifically refers to Article 2.11, concerning ethics and good governance.The FEI has questioned who administers the EFI, following changes in the ad-hoc panel. IOA removed Col Ashok Yadav (retd) from the committee in May, while panel chairperson Yashodhara Raje Scindia and FEI Director (Governance) Francisco Lima subsequently left the panel.The letter states that the FEI is “currently unable to ascertain which person or body is effectively responsible for the administration of the EFI”.The committee later told the court that completing the electoral process could take 150-160 days because of requirements under the new sports law, including restructuring the federation, preparing the Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit roster, holding Athletes’ Commission elections and finalising the electoral college.The FEI has made clear that failure to acknowledge its communication or provide the requested explanation by September 28 will not stop the suspension process. It has also asked the recipient to specify the capacity in which they are responding on behalf of the federation, there.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: The first recorded cricket match in Japan was played 163 years ago in Yokohama, but the sport never quite caught the imagination of the Japanese. Currently, around 7,300 people are registered with the Japan Cricket Association – that’s about 0.00593% of the country’s population!The tech-savvy nation, though, is leaving little to chance in its bid to create awareness about the game. At Korogi Sports Park, the venue for the cricket competition, spectators are handed a leaflet that breaks down the basics of the sport through easy-to-follow visuals.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyIt explains everything from the number of players on the field and fielding positions to umpires’ signals, the difference between a four and a six and how to read a scoreboard. Even the dimensions of the cricket field are put into perspective, with illustrations comparing them with football and baseball fields.Hinata Sato, a baseball mum, arrived with her 10-year-old son Yuto to watch the women’s final on Tuesday. Having watched her son play baseball at the venue, curiosity brought them back to the makeshift cricket stadium.“We have watched videos about cricket. My son wanted to watch it live and the ready reckoner helped him relate to what was happening on the ground. Cricket is really catching up in Japan,” she said.Cuisine lost in translationWhile the Indian men’s cricket team soaked in their first experience of Japanese cuisine by braving the rain in Tokyo to sample some local fare, athletes who have spent more than a week here are already craving for something familiar.Those staying on cruise ships have access to Indian food, but athletes housed in hotels have been exploring Nagoya in search of restaurants serving a taste of home.For one vegetarian athlete, the search was made more difficult by the language barrier and unfamiliarity with Japanese cuisine.“Hum ghaas-phoos khane wale ka struggle bahut hai! articles.title: Lakshya Sen’s eight-point comeback powers India into Asian Games badminton semis
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: When India needed him most, Lakshya Sen rediscovered his fighting spirit.Battling injuries and a prolonged slump in form, the Almora shuttler produced.
articles.body: When India needed him most, Lakshya Sen rediscovered his fighting spirit.Battling injuries and a prolonged slump in form, the Almora shuttler produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of his career, clawing back from 13-19 down in the deciding game against Japan’s Kodai Naraoka to win eight points in a row and seal a stunning victory in the men’s team quarterfinal.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyThat win powered India into the semi-finals as the men swept the host nation 3-0 to assure a second consecutive team medal. The result followed the Indian women’s exit from the competition as they lost 1-3 to the hosts.India had gone into the tie with real concern over the recent form of its top-ranked singles player coming into the Games. Facing a formidable Japanese lineup, the team needed Lakshya to deliver, with the doubles pairing of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the young Ayush Shetty, expected to take care of their respective ties.Lakshya, however, had to dig deep before producing his moment of magic.Trailing 13-19 in the decider, he reeled off eight consecutive points to stun Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19.Satwik and Chirag made it 2-0 for India with a hard-fought win over former world champions Takuro Hoki and Yugo Kobayashi. Ayush then moved India to the brink of victory with a straight-games win over Koki Watanabe, 21-10, 21-19.But the story of the day belonged to Lakshya.He looked out of sorts in the opening game, moving poorly around the court and lacking his usual aggression. A pep talk from chief coach Pullela Gopichand appeared to change the complexion of the contest.Lakshya returned for the second game with renewed energy and immediately took control, racing to a 7-1 lead and never allowing Naraoka to recover as he wrapped up the game 21-5.The momentum shifted again in the decider. Naraoka steadily built an advantage and was sitting comfortably at 19-13, just two points from victory. With India’s hopes resting on him, Lakshya produced the best stretch of the match.At 14-19, he took the risk of playing a cross-court smash to Naraoka’s forehand and followed it with another winner into the backhand corner. The Japanese shuttler then hit into the net before misjudging a line call, allowing Lakshya to draw level at 19-19.At 19-all, Lakshya produced another moment of brilliance, diving full length to retrieve a drop shot and push the shuttle towards the backline to earn match point at 20-19. Naraoka then erred at the net.“It was a memorable victory. Great to see the singles players and Satwik-Chirag win another medal for India. With two Asian Games medals, two Thomas Cup medals and two Badminton Asia medals, it has been a dream period for us. I am confident our team will go the distance,” chief coach Pullela Gopichand told TOI.India will face China in the semi-finals after the latter defeated South Korea 3-2. Indonesia will take on Thailand.The Indian women’s team saw its campaign end against Japan.World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured India’s lone point with a 21-17, 21-16 win over Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto.PV Sindhu lost the opening singles to Akane Yamaguchi 23-21, 18-21, 11-21, while Unnati Hooda went down to Tomoka Miyazaki 16-21, 18-21, leaving Japan 2-0 ahead.Tanvi Sharma then lost the crucial fourth tie to Nozomi Okuhara 12-21, 10-21.The women’s semi-finals will see South Korea face Japan and China play Indonesia.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Connor McDavid, the Edmonton Oilers’ star player and captain, has kept himself busy with the preseason amid the team’s recent win against the Winnipeg Jets. While his wife, Lauren Kyle, has been his cheerleader through every season, she is also a successful interior designer and entrepreneur who runs multiple businesses spanning luxury design, hospitality, and fashion. Ahead of the new season, Connor McDavid’s wife has opened up about her difficult days.Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle opens up about her businesses as he gears up for the new seasonA few weeks ago, in an interview with business major students from the University of Alberta, Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle was asked about how she has let go of the day to day operations of her multiple businesses.To this, Lauren Kyle said, “This has been one of the harder parts for me. When your name is tied to something, it’s natural to want to be involved in everything. What I’ve learned is where I need to stay close to anything that touches the vision, the creative direction, and the overall feeling of the brand.”Connor McDavid’s wife, Lauren Kyle, added, “That’s what ensures everything we put out stays aligned. articles.title: Juggling Chess Olympiad prep and a commentary gig in India: The other side of USA's only female GM Irina Krush
articles.summary: Chess News: NEW DELHI: For most of its history, American women’s chess had a very simple relationship with the Olympiad podium. It did not have one. Not once, in .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: For most of its history, American women’s chess had a very simple relationship with the Olympiad podium. It did not have one. Not once, in over four decades of trying, had the United States women’s team finished among the medals at chess’s biennial team championship.Then, in 2002, Susan Polgar switched her allegiance from Hungary to the United States. Two years later, after stepping away from top-level competition to raise her two sons, she sat down on Board 1 in Calvià, Mallorca, and dragged a young, unheralded American team to silver, second only to China and ahead of a Russian juggernaut that had ruled women’s chess for a generation.It was the first medal of any colour the country had ever won in the women’s category.Bronze followed in Dresden four years later, in 2008. And then, after a wait of 16 years that swallowed many careers, bronze again, this time in Budapest, at a tournament where India finally broke through for gold. Three medals across two decades somehow represented three different eras of American chess.The one name, however, that appears on the scoresheet every single time is that of Irina Krush, the first, and to this day the only, woman to earn the Grandmaster (GM) title while playing for the United States.“I was sort of the main player of my generation,” Krush, who is currently playing in her record-extending 13th Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, said with a small, knowing smile during an exclusive interaction with TimesofIndia.com.A little girl from Soviet UkraineThe story does not begin in America. Krush was born in Odesa, in what was then Soviet Ukraine, and arrived in Brooklyn with her parents when she was five years old. Her father, an amateur player of real quality, taught her the moves.Her first tournament against adults followed when she was six, at the Manhattan Chess Club. She made her first appearance for the United States at the World Youth Championship in Poland at seven. By 11, she was already competing in the US Women’s Championship.At 14, in 1998, she won it. Still, almost three decades on, she remains the youngest champion in the event’s history.Krush’s association with India is a long one too. She fondly recalls playing against a young chess prodigy, Koneru Humpy. In the last few years, her association with India has also included a new part of her profession in chess broadcasting and commentary at the Global Chess League (GCL), a league she participated in during its inaugural 2023 season in Dubai, on a roster built around Magnus Carlsen.You don’t want to look like the fool on the team with Magnus.“It was a chance to play in the same team as Magnus, and it was like a very special opportunity,” Krush added. “I definitely thought that was like a highlight of my chess career.”But a highlight, in her telling, was never the same thing as a comfortable one. “It’s also — you feel the pressure, right? Because you don’t want to look like the fool on the team with Magnus,” she chuckled. “There are two sides to that coin. But overall, it was a very good experience.”She has not played in the league since. What she has done, for the next two seasons, is commentate on it, first in Mumbai and, more recently, in Bengaluru, watching from the other side of the glass.The cost of commentaryThis time, Krush arrived in India with the 46th Chess Olympiad bearing down on her. For more than two decades, the tournament has been the anchor of her competitive identity, and this year, the games in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, were set to begin just two days after her India schedule wrapped up.The commentary booth, for all it has given her, though, has eaten directly into the time she would otherwise have spent getting ready for it.Asked plainly whether she had found any window to play or prepare between broadcasts, she replied: “So far, no. It’s only been a few days, but it’s been so busy. Today, we were asked to appear at the golf thing. So I had to get up at 7:45 in the morning, go to that. Then I had another nap, and then I just had to go here. So it’s a long day. And honestly, I have not had a chance to do much chess for myself at all.”It is a trade she has made with her eyes open, not a complaint dressed up as one. She had spent the months before India trying to bank the form the broadcast schedule was about to interrupt.“I’ve spent the summer playing tournaments, and I just finished a tournament the day before I came here,” she told this website. “There’s definitely been an attempt to try to get myself into good playing condition.”And on the final day, when the commentators were felicitated on the main stage for being the voice of the league, Krush, who became a grandmaster in 2013, barely lingered after the ceremony. She left the arena almost immediately, the next challenge, the Samarkand Olympiad, already waiting.For someone who has spent much of her career playing chess at the highest level, commentary came without formal preparation.“I never did anything special. I don’t have any training in commentary,” she said. “But, you know, it comes kind of naturally for me to talk about chess. It’s something that’s very easy to talk about and get excited about. I like to watch chess.”Her preparation for the booth is less about learning how to commentate and more about doing what she has always done with chess: looking closely at the players and their games.“You definitely try to do some preparation,” she said. “So, you have ways to fill up, you know, give some context for what’s happening. How are the players doing? So, it just requires a little bit of research, you know, to come up with those nuggets that people will find interesting.”But even that preparation changes as a tournament begins to take shape. “At the beginning, you’re doing more general research,” she further noted. “And after the players have started playing against each other, then you’re already more interested in what’s happening in this tournament. What’s the recent results? Not like what happened one year ago in their other matchups.”“As the tournament continues, you start focussing more. What happened in the first half? How do they do again? How are they overall doing in the tournament?” Krush continued.“The tournament itself becomes more of a focus than their history before. Because it’s all now about, like, now you’ve already seen their recent form. So, you focus more on that. Looking at the games is the best part.”The difficulty comes when the chess stops. “The only challenge is, like, maybe sometimes you gotta fill up the time,” she admitted. “You know, the games are over. For me, it’s like, okay, just commenting on the things that are not as exciting for me. You know, just figuring out what to say.“But when we’re on the chess, it’s the easiest.”Eyes on OlympiadThe United States are among the leading teams at the Women’s Chess Olympiad, with a squad featuring Carissa Yip, Alice Lee, Rose Atwell and Tatev Abrahamyan, alongside the most experienced Irina Krush.“It’s like a very nice mix of the young players who are really kind of, they’re not even at their peak yet necessarily, but they’re definitely rising,” Krush said. “And then, okay, like there’s me and Tatev, and we kind of bring a lot of experience to the team. Playing for like 20 years or more for the Olympiad.”That depth, the 42-year-old says, is the product of a sport that barely resembles the one she came up in.“It’s much more competitive (now). There’s more incentive to play chess, more opportunities to play,” the eight-time US women’s champion shared. “We didn’t have the kinds of prizes we have at the US championships 25 years ago. We didn’t have an American Cup. We didn’t have a Cairns Cup. We didn’t have the Cairns Queen chess award for the next woman who’s gonna become a grandmaster in America.”The dividend, she adds, is visible in the players coming up behind her now.“A whole generation of strong girls coming up, with Carissa and Alice being kind of the main ones, but also other young girls who are close to 2400 as well,” Krush acknowledged.In Uzbekistan, the US women’s team made a dream start, but its campaign soon lost momentum. A draw against Uzbekistan was followed by a defeat to India, leaving Krush’s team in 14th place in the rankings heading into the rest day.Any secret sauce?For someone who has now spent two seasons narrating other people’s games for a living, Krush is unsentimental about what the job actually requires.Asked what advice she would give someone hoping to follow her into a commentary booth, she does not reach for a formula.ALSO READ: From uplifting heartbroken team to calling out Chess Olympiad hotel mess: Srinath is India's man to count on“Honestly, there’s just a lot of people who are doing it these days, and everyone brings their own special thing to it, right? So you have different styles. You could be like a top GM and then just start doing commentary. You could be like a different level enthusiast and do commentary,” she concluded, while instinctively running her tongue once again along the outside of her gum. “So I really don’t have any advice except I feel like anyone who loves chess and is pretty good at it can do it.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tampa Bay Rays Secure AL East Crown: 'It's A Tough Division'
articles.summary: Playing in perhaps baseball’s toughest division, the Tampa Bay Rays were the class of the field this season
articles.body: Playing in perhaps baseball's toughest division, the Tampa Bay Rays were the class of the field this season. The thrifty Rays clinched their fifth AL East title with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees in the second game of a day-night doubleheader Tuesday as Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 innings and Yandy Diaz hit a pair of two-run singles. Tampa Bay took the AL East for the first time since 2021 and surpassed that team by three days with the earliest division clincher in team history. The club also won division crowns in the pandemic-shortened 2020 season along with 2010 and 2008, when it reached the World Series and had the franchise's first winning season. "It means a lot," Díaz said through a translator. "It’s a tough division. It’s a competitive division almost every single year. With this group we knew that from the beginning, but we still believed in ourselves every single way. So here we are in Yankee Stadium celebrating and we feel really happy that we got the job done." Tampa Bay (96-61) opened a six-game lead over the second-place Yankees (90-67) with five to play and will be the No. 1 seed with home-field advantage in the American League playoffs. The Rays are two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the best record in the majors and home-field advantage throughout the postseason. The Rays have led the division since June 27 and spent 128 days in first place ahead of the Yankees, who only had Aaron Judge for 66 games due to a fractured right rib and a sore right calf that likely will keep the slugger out of next week’s best-of-three Wild Card Series at home. Tampa Bay initially moved into first place following an 8-5 win over the Chicago White Sox on April 14 but lost the lead despite winning 13 of 18. The Rays regained the lead following a 4-1 win at Boston on May 10 and stayed there until June 13 when they lost seven of 13. "We played really good baseball up to this point," said Rasmussen, who underwent elbow surgery in 2023. "We got off to a little bit of a slow start in April but to play as we have since the beginning of May, this group’s different. We have a lot of fun together. We love being together and we’re trying to spend as much time as we can possibly together." The Rays won their latest division crown after returning to Tropicana Field and going 55-26 at home this season. Last year, Tampa Bay finished 77-85 overall and played home games at Steinbrenner Field, the spring training home of the Yankees, because the domed roof at the Trop was ripped off during Hurricane Milton in October 2024. The Rays secured this AL East title after getting approval on a financing plan that will allow them to build a new stadium in Tampa, Florida, that is expected to open in 2029. "Everything the franchise has been through, to have the Tampa Bay on the chest tonight, the staff, the players for Tampa Bay, all of it, just, it’s really special," president of baseball operations Erik Neander said. After closer Bryan Baker retired Yankees rookie George Lombard Jr. for the final out, the Rays shook hands on the field and exchanged hugs near the dugout to start their celebration. As many Yankees fans left the stadium, Rays fans moved closer to the visitors' dugout and began cheering for the newly minted division champs. Once the party moved inside, the Rays sprayed bubbly and beer on each other while jumping up and down and dancing to loud music in their clubhouse. "I’m very happy because this is a special group," third baseman and AL MVP candidate Junior Caminero said. "When I (went) to spring training (the) first day, I saw this group and (thought), we've got a playoff team this year, and we did it." Rasmussen held the Yankees hitless until Heliot Ramos started the seventh inning with a double to left field. The right-hander exited after walking Jazz Chisholm Jr., but Kevin Kelly retired Austin Wells after allowing Lombard’s run-scoring single. After finishing with three hits during a 2-0 loss in the opener, the Rays all but locked up the division title with a three-run seventh in the nightcap. Taylor Walls had a bunt single and Díaz lined a single to center field for a 4-0 lead. Díaz added another two-run single in the ninth for his AL-leading 175th hit.

articles.body:
Chris Sutton has delivered a scathing assessment of Celtic following their 1-0 defeat to Rangers at Parkhead, describing the Glasgow derby as "men against boys".

Ryan Naderi of the Rangers celebrates scoring the only goal of the game during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and the Rangers at Celtic Park on September 20, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Ryan Naderi's first-half goal proved the difference as Martin O'Neill's side suffered a third successive defeat in all competitions.

Celtic struggled to create anything meaningful despite chasing an equaliser, while Rangers enjoyed the better of the contest and secured all three points.

O'Neill suggested afterwards that the game had been relatively close, but former Celtic striker Sutton strongly disagreed with that assessment.

"Celtic have got big problems. They were smashed by Rangers and that's a concern," Sutton said on Sky Sports.

"Knowing Martin, he'll be greatly concerned.

"I don't like to disagree with him but it wasn't a close game. There was a massive gulf between the teams. I can't actually remember a Celtic team getting such a doing at Celtic Park from a Rangers team, which happened today.

"It looked like Celtic were making it up as they went along.

"Rangers were better in every department.

"It was men against boys, it was the exact same as last week."

articles.title: Netherlands vs Germany: First big test awaits Xavi and Klopp
articles.summary: Netherlands host Germany on Thursday in one of the standout UEFA Nations League games during this international break.The fixture marks a new era for both te...
articles.body:
Netherlands host Germany on Thursday in one of the standout UEFA Nations League games during this international break.

The fixture marks a new era for both teams . Xavi Hernandez is in charge of the Netherlands for the first time, while Jurgen Klopp will be in the German dugout.

The teams have not met since a 2-2 draw in the Nations League in 2024. Germany hold the better overall head-to-head record, winning 18, drawing 18 and losing 12 of their previous 48 matches.

Xavi has a strong squad for this clash, including Liverpool quartet Virgil van Dijk , Ryan Gravenberch , Jeremy Frimpong and Cody Gakpo , Arsenal 's Jurrien Timber and Sunderland 's Brian Brobbey .

The former Barcelona midfielder has said he wants his team to be 'defined by its intensity and ambition', a philosophy he will look to implement during his time in charge.

Thursday's meeting with Germany may be too early for the Netherlands to adapt to his philosophy, but they are expected to show a glimpse of it.

It is unclear whether Xavi will stick with his preferred 4-3-3 formation.

Regardless of the formation, the hosts will look to control possession, move the ball quickly and create numerical advantages.

Klopp also wants his team to play with high intensity, adding further intrigue to this encounter.

The former Liverpool manager has named Arsenal's Kai Havertz , Barcelona's Karim Adeyemi and Brentford 's Kevin Schade in his squad.

Germany will aim to control possession, making the midfield battle one to watch.

Xavi and Klopp share a desire for intensity and possession-based football. It will be intriguing to see which side imposes its style and controls the midfield.

articles.title: Man Utd, Neville and how the media agenda is set
articles.summary: Gary Neville setting the media agenda when it comes to Manchester United is not a new thing.  One instance was in December 2021, after a poor first-half perf...
articles.body:
Gary Neville setting the media agenda when it comes to Manchester United is not a new thing.

The former England defender has called out the team's shortcomings on many previous occasions.

One instance was in December 2021, after a poor first-half performance against a struggling Newcastle side when Ralf Rangnick's side trailed 1-0 at the break.

"They're a bunch of whinge-bags," Neville said at half-time on Sky Sports. "I'll not go into names but they're whinging at each other, arms up in the air complaining about everything.

"There's no pressing, no urgency, the basics of the game."

Edinson Cavani rescued a point at St James' Park, but Neville's comments had already made the headlines.

You only need to look at how the post-match coverage developed after the Fulham draw.

Neville's remarks were put to Michael Carrick at full-time. The United manager said fitness levels of his players were not an issue.

'Neville: That was the worst ever', read the back page of Monday's Daily Telegraph.

'15 minutes of shame', was the lead for the sports section of the Daily Star.

'United boss keeps calm after Neville Ful blast', said the Daily Express.

It was picked up across online media, and discussed at length on radio talk shows - including across the BBC, as evidenced by this piece.

When Neville criticises his former club, it carries weight.

In January, with Ruben Amorim under pressure for poor results, the Portuguese head coach said that "if people cannot handle the Gary Nevilles and the criticisms of everything, we need to change the club".

There always seems to be a strong influence in the media related to the dominant team of a previous era.

For example, throughout the 1990s and 2000s, former Liverpool stars such as Alan Hansen, Mark Lawrenson and Phil Thompson dominated a lot of the conversation.

It stands to reason that members of the all-conquering United squad will now have a leading role in the media.

But for Neville, it is bigger than anyone apart perhaps from Gary Lineker and his Goalhanger production company.

articles.title: Red Bull officially locks in Verstappen’s team-mate for the 2027 season
articles.summary: In a humorous video posted on its social media channels to announce Isack Hadjar's return to the car after three races on the sidelines, Red Bull also took t...
articles.body:
In a humorous video posted on its social media channels to announce Isack Hadjar 's return to the car after three races on the sidelines, Red Bull also took the opportunity to hint at his continued presence alongside Max Verstappen in 2027. Shortly afterwards, the team officially confirmed the line-up, locking it in for next year.

The positive news coincides with the Frenchman's return to the car after missing the last three races due to a wrist injury and being temporarily replaced by Liam Lawson. He will return to his regular duties this weekend in Baku.

Speaking about his continued stay with the team next year, the Frenchman said he is excited to remain with Red Bull , having quickly recognised the scale and ambition of the organisation after joining eight months ago.

He also highlighted the talent within the team and the privilege of racing alongside Verstappen, while stressing his commitment to learning, improving and repaying the faith placed in him by Laurent Mekies and the Milton Keynes-based outfit.

"I am really excited to continue with Oracle Red Bull Racing . I came to this Team eight months ago and immediately understood the scale and ambition of this organisation. There are so many talented people at the factory, and you're aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible Team alongside a four-time World Champion like Max.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the Team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I've been able to justify the faith they've had in me. I'm constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead."

Mekies explains why Red Bull had no doubts about keeping Hadjar for 2027

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies praised the Frenchman's performances since joining the team at the start of the year, highlighting his strong showing both on and off the track despite this being only his second Formula 1 season. He also pointed to the driver's commitment at the factory, where he worked closely with his engineers to help develop the car while continuing to learn and improve.

"We're very excited to continue our journey with Isack. Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.

"From the very beginning, Isack immersed himself in the Team, spending every minute at the factory with his engineers to develop the car, always eager to learn and improve. You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat.

Mekies acknowledged that the period following his injury had been difficult, but stressed that the contract extension reflects the team's strong belief in him. He also expressed his excitement at seeing the Frenchman return to the track, while emphasising the team's shared commitment to achieving its goals for the remainder of the season.

"The period since his injury has been a difficult one for Isack, but this extension is a testament to how much we believe in him and we can't wait to see him back out on track. We still have a lot we want to achieve this season, but it's a great feeling to know that the drivers, engineers and everyone back at the factory are all heading in the same direction, committed and together."

articles.summary: Isack Hadjar has earned a second Red Bull Formula 1 campaign alongside four-time world champion Max Verstappen
articles.body:
Red Bull has confirmed it will field an unchanged Formula 1 driver line-up in 2027, with Isack Hadjar staying put alongside Max Verstappen .

Hadjar stepped up in 2026 after a rookie season at sister team Racing Bulls , and has impressed with his speed in what has historically been a difficult second Red Bull seat.

The Frenchman, who is making his return in Azerbaijan this weekend after missing three races through injury, will stay on board for another campaign in 2027 alongside Verstappen, who recently signed a contract extension to 2030.

"We're very excited to continue our journey with Isack," said Red Bull team boss Laurent Mekies. "Since joining us at the start of the year, he has been superb on and off track, especially considering this is only his second Formula 1 season, which made extending his contract an easy decision.

"From the very beginning, Isack immersed himself in the team, spending every minute at the factory with his engineers to develop the car, always eager to learn and improve. You could see from that first weekend in Melbourne that he handled the step up with remarkable composure and had earned his place in this seat."

Despite sitting out Zandvoort, Monza and Madrid, Hadjar still holds eighth in the standings, boosted by a first Red Bull podium in Monaco to complement his maiden podium in 2025, as well as a streak of seven consecutive top-six finishes in what has largely been F1's third or fourth quickest car.

"I am really excited to continue with Oracle Red Bull Racing," the 21-year-old said. "There are so many talented people at the factory, and you're aware of the privilege of driving for such an incredible team alongside a four-time world champion like Max.

"From the moment I signed, I set out to dedicate myself to the team, and with the support of Laurent and everyone in Milton Keynes, I've been able to justify the faith they've had in me. I'm constantly looking to listen, learn and push myself further every single day, which only makes me more excited about what lies ahead."

Racing Bulls is yet to confirm its own driver line-up for 2027, with incumbents Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad having both impressed this season while the squad also has junior driver Nikola Tsolov waiting in the wings.

articles.title: Cade Cunningham feels ‘weird’ at Detroit Pistons after their move disrupted his career plans
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons are built around Cade Cunningham, but their latest move has just left their star player feeling weird and isolated. Cade Cunningham has s...
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons are built around Cade Cunningham , but their latest move has just left their star player feeling weird and isolated.

Cade Cunningham has started living up to his draft status after a slow start in the NBA, going from strength to strength each season and dragging the Detroit Pistons with him.

He finished fifth in the MVP rankings last season and was in the All-NBA First Team for the first time in his career. The Pistons rode this elite form to 60 wins in the regular season, the most since 2005/06, before falling in the Eastern Conference Semifinals.

Clearly, Cunningham runs the team, so they could ill-afford to alienate him with any decisions. That is exactly what they seem to have done.

Cade Cunningham hurt at Isaiah Stewart trade

Cunningham ran the Pistons, but he was helped by role players like Isaiah Stewart, who was the lynchpin of their bench when the starters sat.

He kept developing his 3PT shot to space the floor, and his switchability onto more nimble players and rim protection made him a complete threat on both ends of the floor.

Pistons, however, wanted financial flexibility to extend Jalen Duren , so they cleared up nearly $30m in future salary by trading Stewart to the Memphis Grizzlies .

The Duren extension talks are getting messy, and Cunningham has also made no effort to hide how he really feels about the Pistons' decision to trade away Stewart.

He said [via Detroit Free Press ]: "That's [Isaiah Stewart] somebody that I planned on playing my whole career with. For him to not be around, it is weird. It feels like I'm a rookie again, like I'm stepping into something new because I don't have him with me."

The Pistons will still be fine, because Cunningham's ceiling is limitless, but this trade, combined with the mess that Duren's extension talks are becoming, shows that all is not well behind the scenes with the Pistons.

These are the kind of decisions the franchise has not had to make in a while because there was no success to speak of, but the dynamics have changed now. They will have to learn the art of building a contender and then managing the stars within that structure.

articles.title: Contagious, confident - the rise of Lewis Koumas
articles.summary: Having made his mark in the early stages of the season at Liverpool, Lewis Koumas will aim to continue his good form with Wales in the Nations League.
articles.body:
By the looks of it, Lewis Koumas is not wasting his time.

It took less than a week of pre-season for the 21-year-old to show new Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola what he could offer.

And it has taken less than a month of the new season for him to show why he has a place in Liverpool's plans.

Now, over the next fortnight, the attacking prospect who is fast becoming an Anfield favourite will attempt to prove what several people in Welsh football have suspected for a long while - that he can have a big impact on the international stage too.

"I feel he's going to be a really important player for us for a number of years," Wales boss Craig Bellamy said before Nations League games with Portugal , Denmark and Norway that will see Koumas share an international stage with the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo and Erling Haaland .

Bellamy is not alone. Wales and Liverpool legend Ian Rush is among a growing number impressed by Koumas' potential, a potential that – despite his recent rise to prominence – has been obvious for a number of years.

Right from the off, in fact. The surname alone brought excitement, given the talents of Lewis' father, former Wales international Jason Koumas .

"Jason was a talented, talented player," says Danny Gabbidon , who played alongside the older Koumas for Wales.

"He could do a bit of everything; technically amazing, he could look after the ball, pass, score fantastic goals. He could just make things happen."

The phrase mercurial midfielder never felt more fitting than for Koumas senior, who won 34 caps and scored 10 goals for Wales but could delight and frustrate in equal measure.

"He could be a bit lazy at times," chuckles Gabbidon when considering a player who was often nonchalance personified.

Indeed, Tranmere Rovers, West Bromwich Albion, Cardiff City and Wigan Athletic fans will all smile at the highlight-reel memories, while having a nagging feeling of what might have been had Koumas had the tenacity to match his talent.

Yet it seems Lewis has some of the qualities his father may have lacked.

"You wouldn't have seen Jason running around like Lewis the other night [for Liverpool against Tottenham ] ," says Gabbidon.

"I kept a close eye on him because I've felt his best position is a striker and I've been keen to see him down the middle.

"To get the chance at a club like Liverpool shows what the manager thinks of him. But it's not just his talent, it's the appetite."

The younger Koumas' attitude is something that has been noted for some time.

Former Liverpool Under-21 head coach Barry Lewtas describes him as "a coach's dream".

"The effort, the will to learn and develop, how he applies himself, it's all there," Lewtas says.

A Liverpool supporter from birth, Koumas has been with the Reds since primary school age, following in the footsteps of his father, who was once a nine-year-old team-mate of Steven Gerrard and Michael Owen.

While Jason moved on to Tranmere without making the breakthrough at Liverpool, Lewis has flourished with the Premier League giants, especially since being pushed from midfield into a forward role at the age of 16.

"That was an important part of his development, getting that exposure of playing deeper, dealing with the ball and the technical side," adds Lewtas.

"But then, when your skill-sets develop, you find the area that suits you best."

Given the influence of then Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp, Lewtas says Koumas' finishing prowess combined with a ferocious attitude towards pressing meant his path was obvious.

"He fitted us and we fitted him," Lewtas says.

By 2024, Klopp had given Koumas his senior debut.

He scored in the FA Cup against Southampton in February 2024 was then an unused substitute as Liverpool beat Chelsea to win the League Cup at Wembley.

There were more than 900 days before his next first-team appearance for Liverpool, with three loan spells in the Championship in between.

At Stoke City, Koumas played under three different managers in a single season, but earned roles under all three during a spell credited for boosting his belief.

He played 25 times for Birmingham City in the first half last season - though managed only seven league starts - before moving on to Hull City and playing an important role in the Tigers' promotion via the play-offs.

Koumas returned to Liverpool in the summer with renewed confidence.

The assumption was that another loan spell beckoned, but Iraola put a stop to such thoughts a week into the club's pre-season trip to the United States.

A Premier League debut followed, as did a first appearance in the Champions League, plus a relentless man-of-the-match performance against Tottenham that enamoured him to the Anfield crowd and seemed to symbolise the demands of the club's new boss.

"He's really matured since making his debut," says Theo Squires, senior football writer at the Liverpool Echo.

"Back then he was just a boy who had caught the eye at academy level as a versatile forward with a keen eye for goal.

"He looks almost unrecognisable physically. Leading the line against Tottenham, he more than held his own and he was a constant nuisance with his pace and never-say-die pressing."

Koumas' energy was described by Iraola as being contagious for the rest of the Liverpool squad, £100m-plus signings included.

"It's been brilliant to see," adds Lewtas. "But it's not just a case of running about and working hard, it's his intelligence. He doesn't just understand what to do, but why he's doing it."

Koumas knows what he is capable of, too.

Matty Jones , the Wales Under-21 head coach, has spoken of the regular meetings he had with Koumas to ensure there was no chance of England nabbing the Wirral-born Welshman.

One ended with Koumas telling Jones: "I'll win you games".

A match-winning, curling finish on his international under-21 debut in 2025 backed up the quiet self-assurance.

Before last June's senior international friendlies, Koumas said Wales fans had not seen "anything from me yet".

He pointed that having played only cameo roles for Wales, he needed to "work harder and show a little bit more to get the trust of the gaffer".

He duly scored his first international goal against Ghana .

"He's been there in every squad I've announced but I felt in the summer, he turned," says Bellamy. "When he came on against Ghana, he changed it completely – and he's a player who's capable of that.

"He's just coming into his own now and kicking on again – and to be the top player we expect him to be, that has to be the case."

Both club and international bosses agree there is more to work on, but also that there is more to come.

Wales will hope that he can make further strides during a demanding Nations League campaign which begins against Portugal in Lisbon on Thursday.

"He knows there is a higher ceiling," says Lewtas.

"Knowing Lewis' appetite for things, he won't be worried about it, he'll be looking forward to it."

articles.title: Mirabai Chanu wins Asian Games silver as Ri breaks weightlifting record
articles.summary: Chanu finally clinches an elusive Asian Games medal in Japan and Ri Song-gum wins North Korea’s first gold.
articles.body:
North Korean weightlifter Ri Song Gum has broken three world records en route to winning gold in the women’s 49kg (108lbs) competition, which saw India’s Mirabai Chanu win an elusive Asian Games medal by finishing second.

Ri gave North Korea its first gold of the games in Nagoya, Japan, on Wednesday, joining an elite club of four weightlifters who have won three Asian Games gold medals.

The 28-year-old hauled 94kg above her head in the opening snatch discipline – the first official segment of the competition where athletes lift a barbell from the floor to an overhead position in a single motion. The lift was 1kg heavier than the previous world record of 93kg.

Ri followed it up by breaking the world record twice in the 115kg clean and jerk – a two-part movement where a barbell is lifted from the floor to the shoulders and then pushed overhead. The 4ft-7in (139.7cm) weightlifter hoisted 116kg and 121kg above her head.

Ri’s total lift of 215kg obliterated the old world record total by 7kg.

She is the fourth lifter, and first woman, to win three Asian Games weightlifting golds and joined Iran’s Mohammad Nassiri (1966-74), South Korea’s Kim Tae-hyun (1990-98) and Iran’s Behdad Salimi (2010-18), who all won three gold medals. No athlete has won four weightlifting gold medals.

In the same category, India’s Chanu finally won an Asian Games medal at the third time of asking. She won a silver medal at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021.

The 32-year-old is India’s most decorated weightlifter, with three Commonwealth gold medals and a silver to her name, along with multiple global titles.

She lifted a total of 198kg after a snatch of 87kg and a clean and jerk of 111kg, while Indonesia’s Diana Tri Wijayana took bronze with a total of 191kg, comprising 88kg and 103kg.

Chanu’s silver also ended India’s 28-year wait for a weightlifting medal at the games since Karnam Malleswari won silver in 1998.

Ri joined an elite club of just four weightlifters who have won three Asian Games gold medals [Dita Alangkara/AP]
