articles.title: Qatar’s Dakar Rally champ Nasser Al-Attiyah wins Asian Games shooting gold
articles.summary: Al-Attiyah is the first person to win a gold medal at the Games in the same year as his Dakar Rally triumph.
articles.body:
Qatar’s Nasser Al-Attiyah has completed a unique double by capturing a shooting gold medal at the Asian Games in the same year that he won the Dakar Rally.

The 55-year-old was part of the Qatar men’s skeet team that took gold on Wednesday ahead of Kuwait and India in Nagoya, Japan.

It was his third Asian Games gold after triumphs in 2002 and 2010 and his sixth medal at the Games overall.

He also won skeet bronze at the 2012 London Olympics.

Al-Attiyah added his latest medal to his collection of driving accolades, which includes six Dakar Rally titles.

He secured the latest one this year alongside Belgian codriver Fabian Lurquin.

At the wheel of a Dacia, he had to avoid only a final day slip-up to top the podium after bringing his career tally of stage wins to 50 the previous day.

articles.title: España busca cantar los 40 en un templo como Wembley
articles.standfirst: 1XBET le otorga un ligero favoritismo a la Selección en su visita a Inglaterra para arrancar la Nations League
articles.summary: 1XBET le otorga un ligero favoritismo a la Selección en su visita a Inglaterra para arrancar la Nations League
articles.body: España arranca una nueva edición de la Nations League con la etiqueta de vigente campeona del mundo y un reto tan simbólico como histórico. La Selección visita este sábado un templo como Wembley con el objetivo de prolongar la mayor racha de partidos oficiales consecutivos sin perder en la historia del fútbol de selecciones. Una racha que comenzó el 15 de junio de 2023, precisamente en la Nations League, cuando España derrotó a Italia en las semifinales antes de conquistar el título frente a Croacia. Desde entonces, la Selección se ha medido a las mejores selecciones del planeta y ninguna ha conseguido derrotarla durante los 90 o 120 minutos reglamentarios. Entre sus grandes victorias destacan las conseguidas ante Inglaterra en la final de la Eurocopa 2024 y Argentina en la final del Mundial 2026. Es cierto que Portugal consiguió imponerse en la final de la Nations League 2025, pero lo hizo en la tanda de penaltis después de que el encuentro terminara en empate durante el tiempo reglamentario. Por ello, España llega a Wembley con las apuestas deportivas de su lado. En total, España acumula ya 39 partidos oficiales consecutivos sin conocer la derrota. Una cifra que supone la mayor racha de la historia del fútbol de selecciones. El desafío es ahora cantar los 40 en uno de los escenarios más emblemáticos del planeta y hacerlo, además, ante una Inglaterra a la que ya consiguió derrotar en su propio estadio en la última visita de 2018. Los precedentes más recientes también sonríen al combinado español, que volvió a imponerse a los ingleses en la final de la Eurocopa 2024. Las mejores casas de apuestas también reflejan el equilibrio de un encuentro que enfrenta a dos de las grandes potencias del fútbol internacional. 1XBET sitúa a España como ligera favorita con una cuota de 2.45, mientras que el empate cotiza a 3.30. Escenario que le permitiría conservar este invicto y llegar a esos 40 partidos seguidos sin perder. Más allá de los números, Wembley supondrá una prueba de máxima exigencia para una Selección que lleva más de tres años resistiendo ante todos sus rivales en partido oficial. El estreno en la Nations League tendrá, por tanto, un premio añadido para España. Más allá de comenzar con buen pie una competición que ya conquistó en 2023, el equipo de Luis de la Fuente puede convertir una cifra redonda en otro capítulo de su extraordinaria etapa como seleccionador nacional. Estos 39 partidos ya forman parte de la historia... pero no se conforma. Quiere prolongar esta racha hasta el infinito y hacerlo ante Inglaterra, uno de los rivales que ya ha sufrido el dominio español en este ciclo, añadiría todavía más valor a una racha que no parece tener techo.

articles.title: Matteo Moretto avisa sobre el futuro de Sergio Camello
articles.standfirst: El delantero está en el radar de clubes importantes de España, Italia y México
articles.summary: El delantero está en el radar de clubes importantes de España, Italia y México
articles.body: El mercado de fichajes empieza a moverse mucho antes de que se abra oficialmente la ventana de enero. Matteo Moretto desveló en La Pizarra varios nombres que están despertando interés, con especial atención a Sergio Camello, cuyo rendimiento y situación contractual le colocan como uno de los futbolistas a seguir. "El rendimiento le ha llevado a ser objetivo de clubes importantes de España, Italia y México. Camello está jugando muy bien, marcando goles", explicó Moretto. Más allá de su rendimiento sobre el terreno de juego, hay un factor contractual que aumenta el atractivo de Camello en el mercado. "El detalle que le convierte en un pepino a nivel de mercado es el tema de que acaba contrato en 2027", señaló Moretto. Una situación que puede provocar movimientos alrededor del delantero en las próximas ventanas: "Puede ser y va a ser un futbolista importante en el mercado de enero y verano". Moretto también aportó un detalle sobre la situación contractual de Roberto Fernández. "Si llega un equipo de la Premier y quiere fichar a Roberto Fernández la cláusula sube. También ha subido por haber ido a la selección", explicó. El periodista añadió que "ese contrato fue firmado por Fran Garagarza". El seguimiento internacional también alcanza a dos jóvenes centrales que están destacando en Segunda División. Moretto puso sobre la mesa los nombres de Bourama Dembele y Zamorano. "Hay dos chicos que juegan en Segunda División y están destacando y ojeadores de las cinco grandes ligas les están viendo y siguiendo en directo", reveló. Los dos futbolistas señalados son "Bourama Dembelé, de 19 años, del Granada, y Holmes Zamorano, del Girona, de 17 años". Dos centrales jóvenes que, según la información de Moretto, ya están siendo observados de cerca por clubes de las principales ligas europeas.

articles.title: China’s swimming prodigy Yu Zidi bags third gold in Asian Games record
articles.summary: The 13-year-old beat the previous 400m Asian Games record, set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014, by about 4.5 seconds.
articles.body:
China’s 13-year-old swimming sensation Yu Zidi has completed a hat-trick of Asian Games golds with a dominant victory in the 400m individual medley, two years before the Los Angeles Olympics.

The schoolgirl powered home in an Asian Games-record 4 minutes 28.56 seconds (04:28.56) on Wednesday to make it a clean sweep of her three individual events in Tokyo, following victories in the 200m butterfly and 200m individual medley, also in games-record times.

She beat the previous 400m games record set by China’s Ye Shiwen in 2014 by approximately 4.5 seconds.

It was the fourth-fastest time in the world this year, with world record-holder Summer McIntosh owning the top three.

With the next Olympics two years away, Yu is shaping up to be a major medal contender at the 2028 Los Angeles Games.

Last year, she became the youngest medallist at the World Aquatics Championships, where she won bronze for China’s relay team at the age of 12, and has since been earmarked for success in the swimming world.

At the same championship, Yu finished fourth by a small margin in three individual events.

In March, the teen sensation built on her growing reputation with a 200m butterfly victory over seven-time American Olympic medallist Regan Smith at the China Swimming Open.

At the Asian Games, Yu has dominated the pool and showed another glimpse of her immense talent in the 400m individual medley, where she took the lead from the start and finished 3.95 seconds clear of silver medallist Ke Wenxi of China, with Japan’s Mio Narita finishing third.

In addition to grabbing international headlines, Yu has become a sensation at home following her Asian Games exploits.

The story of her introduction to competitive swimming after being spotted by a coach at a water park, and her struggle with interviews, has gone viral on local social media platforms.

At the games, Yu was asked by the media whether answering questions was the hardest part of competing. She replied, with a giggle: “Every time I just want to float off somewhere else.”

articles.title: What if AEW's Jon Moxley Never Left WWE?
articles.summary: Jon Moxley has been vital to the rise and success of AEW since the very beginning.
articles.body:
Jon Moxley has been vital to the rise and success of AEW since the very beginning.

From the moment he made his triumphant arrival at All Elite Wrestling's premiere pay-per-view Double or Nothing 2019, Moxley was prominently positioned as one of the faces of the franchise. He was a centerpiece in the early days of Dynamite and helped carry the company through its pandemic period the very next year.

Even today, Moxley remains an important piece of the AEW puzzle as he prepares to challenge Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship in the main event of All Out while simultaneously reigning as AEW Continental champion.

All of that begs the question of what would happened had Moxley never left WWE.

Not only would the career trajectory of the artist formerly known as Dean Ambrose been drastically different, the seismic shift the pro wrestling landscape experienced with the launch of AEW in 2019 may have looked a little different as well.

By the time Dean Ambrose departed WWE in the spring of 2019, his Shield cohorts were already multi-time world champions. Ambrose accomplished quite a bit in his seven years on the main roster had only one reign as world champ to his credit.

His WWE Championship reign lasted a measly three months in 2016, and despite being drafted first by SmackDown that summer, he was never truly portrayed as "the guy" in the company, even on his own brand. He was never booked remotely as strong as Seth Rollins or Roman Reigns.

After his main event push was cut short, Ambrose was demoted to the midcard while Rollins and Reigns remained fixtures at the top of the card. The Lunatic Fringe spent the last three years of his run floating around the Intercontinental Championship scene and latching onto short-lived Shield reunions for relevance.

Ambrose's bad booking made it abundantly clear he had hit his ceiling and that those in charge at the time didn't view or value him as highly as they should have. Had he stayed, his status on the show very likely wouldn't have changed and he would have become more of a stepping stone.

Leaving was the only way he could reinvent himself as a main event attraction.

Being Elevated by the Shield and Bloodline Lore

Dean Ambrose's long-awaited heel turn at the end of 2018 was one of WWE's biggest creative fumbles during that period. It was so horribly handled that the company virtually had no choice but to abandon his heel run within a matter of months.

He even reunited with Rollins and Reigns right before WrestleMania 35, but that was largely because everyone was aware Ambrose was on his way out and one last Shield reunion was a must. Odds are he would have stayed in the heel role had he re-signed with the company.

Reigns turning heel himself was inevitable, as was the ill-fated Performance Center/ThunderDome era of WWE due to the looming pandemic. The Tribal Chief would have arrived all the same, and for as intertwined as Reigns and Rollins have been since 2020, Ambrose would have very much been in that mix as well.

A full-fledged feud with Reigns over the Universal Championship would have elevated Ambrose to the main event scene, albeit temporarily. After that was over (and Ambrose undoubtedly would have lost those wars), he would have been back to pulling midcard duty.

Sticking around solely so he could be involved in the excessive Shield and Bloodline lore wouldn't have been worth it.

Beyond the obvious rematch with Reigns (they only ever went one-on-one at Survivor Series 2015), Ambrose would have a very limited number of fresh faces to work with in the years following his hypothetical contract extension.

Cody Rhodes is perhaps the most notable name, though they crossed paths fairly frequently in the final months of 2013 while the Rhodes family was feuding with The Shield and The Authority. Ambrose and Rhodes were both on the AEW roster from 2019 through early 2022 but never did battle during that time.

Although a formal feud eluded Ambrose and Drew McIntyre, they did have a few matches against each other on Raw between 2018 and 2019. Due to the vast amount of releases post-pandemic, the roster was light on star power, so there weren't too many people remaining on the roster that Ambrose didn't already face off against.

Even familiar faces who returned years later, such as Edge and CM Punk, Ambrose has had matches with in AEW. Bron Breakker, Oba Femi, Je'Von Evans and others currently dominate the WWE landscape, but with where Ambrose was positioned on the card, most of those matches may have been booked as squashes and not in Ambrose's favor.

Would Other WWE Top Talents Have Also Stayed Put?

Dean Ambrose's WWE exit was also significant at the onset of 2019 because it marked one of the first major departures from the company in some time, at least at that level.

With this being right around when AEW launched, there weren't many places for talent to go to and make as much money or be as successful. CM Punk previously walked out in 2014 but retired from wrestling all together until 2014, while guys like Dolph Ziggler re-signed for lucrative contracts even if meant consistent creative satisfaction wasn't guaranteed.

It's worth noting that Ambrose's WWE contract simply expired, so he wasn't bound to a non-compete clause and didn't have to negotiate for an early release. Despite that, many Superstars went on to publicly request their releases but were denied because of the threat AEW was now posing.

Creatively, WWE was in a pretty poor state in 2019, so some stars were going to leave regardless, but Ambrose's situation definitely encouraged others to follow in his footsteps and journey into the unknown, even without AEW not being completely established at that point.

A world-renowned name himself, Chris Jericho's signing gave AEW instant credibility, but Ambrose a.k.a. Jon Moxley was a much hotter commodity when it put pen to paper with the promotion. His success in AEW had to have played a role in the illustrious likes of Punk and Bryan Danielson giving it a shot just two years later.

AEW was built around The Elite from the get-go, but they needed to fill out their roster with other established stars from across the wrestling world to send the message that they were the real deal.

A world-renowned name himself, Chris Jericho's signing gave AEW instant credibility. One of the best decisions the company made early on was making him the inaugural world champ, and Jericho being on board was arguably the difference maker in landing AEW a television deal despite the promotion being unproven.

Dean Ambrose, now rechristened as Jon Moxley, was a much hotter commodity when he put pen to paper with the promotion in May 2019. Jericho held the top title before anyone else, but that was so Moxley could gradually be built up to beat him in February 2020.

As previously noted, Moxley was the man AEW depended on more than anyone when the world went into lockdown due to the pandemic that year. He ruled Dynamite as AEW World champ with pride and constantly stepped up in situations when wrestlers went down to injury in the years that followed.

His success in AEW had to have played a role in the illustrious likes of Punk and Bryan Danielson giving it a shot in the summer of 2021. AEW would have eventually excelled regardless, but they found their footing much quicker thanks to Moxley being in the right place at the right time.

Jon Moxley was the focal point of AEW's main event scene for the first two years, and from there, he further expanded into New Japan Pro-Wrestling and later formed Blackpool Combat Club with Bryan Danielson and William Regal.

In other words, Moxley was and still is consistently involved in something of note. That wouldn't at all have been the case had he not left WWE in 2019.

Even had his run not ended then, Moxley was always destined for AEW, simply based on his booking, style, WWE's limitations and the landscape in general. It's possible he would have stayed with WWE for the full five years after re-signing or been released sooner if the company didn't feel he was worth what they were paying him.

AEW was organically going to gain steam with or without Moxley and their surge in popularity was undeniably going to appeal to someone like him, especially if his role in WWE stayed stagnant. He would have ended up in the same spot at some point, but it was way more beneficial for him, AEW and wrestling as a whole for his career resurgence to happen when it did.

Whether he'll ever resurface in WWE is anyone's guess, but if the outstanding in-ring year he's had and the latest AEW World Championship opportunity he has coming up at All Out are any indications, there really is no reason for him to call anywhere else but AEW home.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Ranking the 20 Best Sports Families of All Time
articles.summary: Between the Manning brothers, the Williams sisters and plenty of father and son/daughter combos, there have been a number of iconic families throughout sports history.
articles.body:
Between the Manning brothers, the Williams sisters and plenty of father and son/daughter combos, there have been a number of iconic families throughout sports history.

As we tried to compare home runs, touchdowns, heavyweight belts, three-point buckets, goals and races won, coming up with any sort of mathematical formula for ranking the greatest sports families wasn't feasible.

However, one question reigned supreme when trying to sort out the hierarchy: How incomplete would your verbal history of the sport be if you left out that family?

Whether their legacy is tied to Hall of Fame plaques, championship rings, record-setting statistics, cultural impact or some combination of those and more, these families boast multiple athletes you've almost certainly heard of, even if you've never intentionally watched that particular sport. (In some cases, that might not ring true because they played so long ago. But you get the idea.)

As a general rule of thumb, more family members mean more consideration in the ranking. Multiple impact players were a must. For instance, you won't find LeBron and Bronny James on this list, nor Hank and Tommie Aaron. With that said, we've got several twosomes in our top five, so having three or more athletes in the family was more of a potential perk than a prerequisite or automatic boost.

Before we start counting down our top 20, we'll first present the honorable mentions who narrowly missed the cut.

All notes relating to point shares, win shares, approximate value or bWAR are according to Sports Reference.

Dick Van Arsdale and Tom Van Arsdale : Only one family has produced two players who rank in the top 200 all-time in points scored in the NBA. They also happened to be twins. Neither is in the Hall of Fame, but each was a three-time All-Star who lasted 12 years in the Association.

Reggie Miller and Cheryl Miller : Had there been a WNBA when Cheryl graduated college and/or had knee injuries not prevented her from playing professionally, this would have been a different story. As it was, she was a three-time national player of the year at USC, while Reggie was one of the NBA's greatest three-point shooters (pre-Stephen Curry, anyway).

Vitali Klitschko and Wladimir Klitschko : The Ukrainian brothers held all of the world heavyweight titles simultaneously for more than two years without ever fighting each other. Quite the achievement. However, neither is generally considered one of the 50 best boxers of all time, so they fell outside our top 20.

Paul Waner and Lloyd Waner : Paul was a four-time All-Star, a three-time batting champ and the 1927 NL MVP. Lloyd hit .316 in his career but made only one All-Star Game. Both are in the Hall of Fame with a combined 5,611 hits.

Ronde Barber and Tiki Barber : Ronde was a sensational cornerback who racked up 47 interceptions and more than 1,250 tackles in his Hall of Fame career. Meanwhile, Tiki made three straight Pro Bowls late in his career after he finally shed the label of being fumble-prone.

Klay Thompson and Mychal Thompson : Mychal was the No. 1 overall pick in 1978 and went on to score nearly 13,000 points in the NBA. His son, Klay, became the much bigger star as one half of the Splash Bros. At some point during the 2026-27 season, he will likely become just the third player to reach 3,000 career three-pointers.

Pau Gasol and Marc Gasol : Pau was named Rookie of the Year in 2001-02, with s ix All-Star Game selections, more than 20,000 points and a place in the Hall of Fame. Marc's legacy wasn't quite that lasting, but he was a three-time All-Star and a one-time Defensive Player of the Year.

Calvin Hill and Grant Hill : Dad was a four-time Pro Bowl running back. Son was a seven-time All-Star enshrined in the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame. Each was named Rookie of the Year amid a phenomenal first six professional seasons before injuries suffered at the age of 28 robbed them both of what might have been legendary careers.

Henrik Sedin and Daniel Sedin : Aside from maybe tennis' Bob and Mike Bryan, no sports brothers have been more inseparable than these twins who spent their entire 17-year career together in Vancouver. Both Hall of Famers eclipsed 1,000 career points, including 340 instances in which one assisted on the other's goal.

Sandy Alomar, Sandy Alomar Jr. and Roberto Alomar : Sandy Sr. was a respectable middle infielder who carved out a 15-year career. But his sons were special, combining for 18 All-Star Games and 11 Gold Gloves. Sandy Jr. was AL Rookie of the Year in 1990. Roberto was voted into the Hall of Fame in 2011.

Eric Staal, Marc Staal and Jordan Staal : Say this much for the Staal brothers: If you've watched any NHL in the past two decades, you've likely seen at least one of them in action. The trio has combined for 3,904 games played, with Eric making the biggest impact with more than 1,000 points scored.

The Actors : Vladimir Guerrero Sr., Vladimir Guerrero Jr.

The Accolades : 1 Hall of Famer, 15 All-Star Selections, 1 MVP, 10 Silver Sluggers, 1 Gold Glove, 2 Home Run Derby Titles, 86.5 bWAR

To date, only one family has multiple players enshrined in Cooperstown. Whether Lloyd "Little Poison" Waner really deserves a plaque next to Paul "Big Poison" Waner is debatable at best.

The Guerreros might be joining that club in 15 to 20 years.

Vlad Sr., a lifetime .318 hitter with 449 home runs, is already in the Hall of Fame. He earned nine All-Star selections and eight Silver Sluggers as noted above.

Dad Guerrero had 10 seasons with at least 27 home runs and more than 100 runs batted in. He came painstakingly close to joining the exclusive 40/40 club with 39 home runs and 40 stolen bases in 2002. He also became a superstar during the peak of the steroids era without ever once getting implicated in that mess.

Vlad Jr. had an underwhelming 2026 campaign, but he has been an All-Star in each of the last six seasons and would have won AL MVP in 2021 were it not for Shohei Ohtani's two-way brilliance.

Jr. is closing in on 200 career home runs, but he's only 27 years old and just one season into his 14-year, $500 million contract. The Blue Jays certainly bet big on him staying great for many years to come, hoping he'll one day become the eighth player in MLB history with 3,000 hits and 500 home runs.

(Vlad. Sr. also had a brother, Wilton, who spent eight seasons in the majors. As a career journeyman with a bWAR of negative-1.8, though, including him wouldn't have helped the ranking.)

The Accolades : 1 Hall of Famer, 6 All-Star Games, 5 Gold Gloves, 125.6 bWAR

The owner of the greatest fastball in baseball history is wide open to debate.

But the greatest knuckleball pitcher? It's Phil Niekro, and it's not even close.

Knucksie pitched into his late 40s, amassing 318 wins and 3,342 strikeouts in his 5,404 innings pitched, ranking fourth in MLB history in the latter department.

There were also plenty of walks, wild pitches and passed balls along the way, as even he often couldn't know where the wind would take that mischievous ball. He did throw a no-hitter in 1973, adding to his 45 career shutouts.

While Phil was the clear-cut best knuckleball pitcher ever, his younger brother Joe surely ranks in the top 10 with 221 wins and 1,747 strikeouts of his own. (That's a combined 539 wins and 5,089 strikeouts for the Niekro Bros.)

Joe also had an uncommonly long career spanning 22 seasons, though he fell nearly 2,000 innings shy of his brother's mark.

The 1979 campaign was their combined magnum opus. Each won 21 games—Phil doing so for an Atlanta team that went 66-94—and each received votes for the NL Cy Young Award.

The Actors : J.J. Watt, T.J. Watt, Derek Watt

The Accolades : 13 Pro Bowls, 9-Time First-Team All-Pro, 4-Time AP Defensive Player of the Year, 229.5 sacks, 63 forced fumbles, 247 Approximate Value

This family has no Pro Football Hall of Fame busts yet, but some are likely coming soon.

J.J. will become eligible for the first time in the Class of 2028. He should get in with room to spare on his first time on the ballot. He is one of just nine players to be named Defensive Player of the Year multiple times. He's one of only three (along with Lawrence Taylor and Aaron Donald) to receive that honor three times. Injuries put a real damper on what should have been some peak years, but he was a force of nature when healthy.

T.J. is still going strong in the NFL and already entered 2026 with more career sacks (115) than J.J. (114.5). He got 22.5 of those sacks in 2021, tying the (since-broken) record for most in a single season. (And, let's be real, Watt getting 22.5 in 15 games was more impressive than Myles Garrett getting 23.0 in 17 games in 2025.) He has been named a Pro Bowler in each of the past eight seasons, received votes for DPOY in five of those years and won it in 2021.

As far as Derek goes, fullbacks haven't exactly been en vogue in the NFL for decades. He did play in 110 games over seven seasons, scored three touchdowns and got the occasional tackle on special teams.

The Actors : Phil Esposito, Tony Esposito

The Accolades : 2 Hall of Famers, 16 All-Star selections, 2 Stanley Cups, 5 Ross Trophies, 3 Vezina Trophies, 2 Hart Trophies, 342.4 point shares

Phil Esposito was born 14 months before his brother Tony. You can probably imagine the backyard bickering that led the younger of the two to tend the net while big bro worked on his slapshot.

In this case, though, iron sharpened iron. Each brother became one of the best in the world at his craft.

Phil amassed 717 goals and 873 assists in his 18-year career, leading the NHL in points in five seasons. He ranks seventh all-time in goals and is one of just six players with at least 700 goals and 700 assists in an NHL career.

Tony also led the NHL in a category five times. His specialty was preventing points from happening. He faced the most shots and recorded the most saves in five of his 16 seasons. He ranks 11th in NHL history in regular-season wins (423) and fifth in saves with nearly 25,000.

Tony never won a Stanley Cup, but he came close in both 1971 and 1973. Phil won his in 1970 and 1972.

The Actors : Ray Boone, Bob Boone, Bret Boone, Aaron Boone

The Accolades : 10 All-Star Selections, 11 Gold Gloves, 2 Silver Sluggers, 2 World Series, 89.6 bWAR

Individually, none of the Boones were exactly all-time greats.

Bob had arguably the best playing career of the bunch. Aaron's second career as manager of the New York Yankees has certainly generated plenty of attention. However, none of the four is knocking on Cooperstown's door for inclusion.

This family is quite the "whole is greater than the sum of its parts" situation. With four players spanning three generations, they were all selected to at least one All-Star Game.

Bob was a four-time All-Star and a seven-time Gold Glover during his 19-year career as a catcher.

Bob's older son, Bret, made three All-Star teams and earned the other four Gold Gloves and both Silver Sluggers listed above. Alongside Ichiro Suzuki, Bret led the 2001 Mariners to 116 regular-season wins, hitting 37 home runs and driving in a league-best 141 runs.

Bob's father, Ray, was a two-time All-Star, peaking in the mid-1950s with three consecutive years receiving votes for AL MVP (albeit never placing higher than eighth)

Bob's younger son, Aaron, was an All-Star in 2003, a few months prior to his iconic walk-off home run off Tim Wakefield in Game 7 of the ALCS.

The Actors : Howie Long, Chris Long, Kyle Long

The Accolades : 1 Hall of Famer, 11 Pro Bowls, 3 Super Bowls, 221 Approximate Value

Prior to what has been more than three decades in the Fox studio alongside Terry Bradshaw, Howie Long was a wrecking ball of a defensive end for the Raiders.

The NFL didn't officially track tackles until the latter half of his career, but Howie recorded 91.5 sacks over his 13 seasons in the league, which still ranks among the top 100 all-time in that category. In addition to eight Pro Bowls, he was named first-team All-Pro in both 1984 and 1985 and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2000.

Two of his three sons followed in his footsteps to the line of scrimmage. Chris was also a defensive end, while Kyle was an offensive lineman.

Chris had 70 career sacks and matched his father's mark of 15 forced fumbles. He has the most Super Bowl rings of the bunch, earning one with the New England Patriots in 2016 and another the following year with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Kyle had the potential to be the greatest of the Longs, earning Pro Bowl honors in each of his first three seasons in the NFL. Unfortunately, he played in just 30 more games before retiring after his age-31 campaign due to a litany of injuries.

The Actors : Ken Griffey Sr., Ken Griffey Jr.

The Accolades : 1 Hall of Famer, 16 All-Star Selections, 2 World Series, 2 All-Star Game MVPs (one apiece), 118.3 bWAR

Junior did most of the heavy lifting for this father/son duo on his way to Cooperstown.

He hit 630 career home runs. He won 10 Gold Gloves and seven Silver Sluggers, plus three Home Run Derbies.

Before the Madden video game franchise started putting players on the cover in the early 2000s, we had Ken Griffey Jr. Presents Major League Baseball in 1994 and Major League Baseball Featuring Ken Griffey Jr. in 1998.

Throw in the signature backwards hat, and "The Kid" was an icon for an entire generation of baseball fans.

Senior was a three-time All-Star in his own right and played a key role for the World Series-winning Reds in both 1975 and 1976. (Junior never got a ring.)

Dad Griffey hit .296 for his career with 152 home runs and 200 stolen bases. He was worth 34.5 wins above replacement in his 19-year career, per Baseball Reference . Eventually, he played alongside his son in Seattle during his final two seasons.

The Actors : Joe DiMaggio, Dom DiMaggio, Vince DiMaggio

The Accolades : 1 Hall of Famer, 22 All-Star Selections, 9 World Series, 3 MVPs, 129.7 bWAR

Joltin' Joe DiMaggio is generally regarded as one of the 25 greatest players in MLB history.

He is one of only 13 players to have won at least three MVPs. He did so despite sacrificing three seasons from age 28 to 30 to serve in the U.S. Army Air Forces during World War II. He might be an undisputed top-five big leaguer if we didn't have to guess what he could have done in those three seasons.

Did you know the Yankee Clipper was only responsible for 13 of this sibling group's 22 All-Star selections?

Dom—who also missed out on three prime years for military service from 1943-45—was a seven-time All-Star who amassed 1,680 career hits. To this day, he is just outside the top 500 on that all-time leaderboard. He might be in the top 200 alongside Joe had he played those three years.

Vince was a free-swinging, two-time All-Star who hit 125 home runs while "leading" the National League in strikeouts in six of his 10 seasons.

Maybe the coolest DiMaggio nugget: When Joe won his second MVP in 1941, Vince received 10 votes for NL MVP and Dom received one vote for AL MVP. That has to be the only time that three family members received MVP votes in the same season, right?

The Actors : Shannon Sharpe, Sterling Sharpe

The Accolades : 2 Hall of Famers, 13 Pro Bowls, 7-time first-team All-Pro, 3 Super Bowls, 186 approximate value

Sterling's career ended far too soon, truncated by a serious neck injury, but he sure made the most of his seven seasons in the NFL. He led the league in receptions three times, receiving touchdowns twice and receiving yards once, averaging 85 catches and 1,162 yards per season.

Had he been able to play into his 30s, he would have been well on his way to going down as one of the 10 greatest wide receivers in NFL history.

Sterling's younger brother, Shannon, managed to play 14 seasons and became one of the 10 greatest tight ends of all time.

He's fifth in career receiving yards (10,060) and eighth in career receiving touchdowns (62) among tight ends. When he retired, he was the undisputed No. 1 in both categories. He walked so the likes of Tony Gonzalez and Antonio Gates could eventually run.

The Sharpe brothers combined for 1,410 receptions, 18,194 yards and 127 touchdowns en route to two busts in Canton.

The Accolades : 18 Pro Bowls, 10-time First-Team All-Pro, 4 Super Bowls, 256 Approximate Value

Long before Travis Kelce started dating Taylor Swift, he was already one of the best tight ends in football history.

From 2016-22, he had seven consecutive seasons with at least 1,000 receiving yards. Overall, he's now north of 13,000 yards and 80 touchdowns, closing in on 1,100 career receptions. With a respectable run through the 2026 season, he should finish top 20 all time—not just among tight ends, but among all players—in each of those three categories.

Travis is responsible for 11 of the brothers' 18 Pro Bowls, as well as three of the Super Bowls. He's now married to one of the most famous people on the planet.

But it's Jason who was at the epicenter of the most controversial play design in recent history: the tush push.

A dominant center who repeatedly graded as one of the best offensive linemen in the sport, the Eagles decided to start running their offense through him. He earned first-team All-Pro honors in six of his final seasons before calling it a career and pivoting to podcasts and commercials.

Can't imagine it'll be long after Travis retires before there's a KelceCast as the Thursday night counterpart to the ManningCast.

The Actors : Maurice Richard, Henri Richard

The Accolades : 2 Hall of Famers, 19 Stanley Cups, 23 All-Star Selections, 1 Hart Trophy, 224 win shares

The Sedin twins narrowly missed our top 20, largely because they never managed to bring a Stanley Cup to Vancouver.

The Richard Brothers, on the other hand, have had their names chiseled into the bands of that iconic trophy a slightly ridiculous number of times.

Born 15 years apart, though, only five of their 19 combined championships overlapped.

Maurice had already won three Stanley Cups with the Montreal Canadiens by the time Henri made it into the NHL. They proceeded to win five in a row during the five seasons when "Rocket" and "Pocket Rocket" joined forces.

Henri won six more after Maurice retired and is the NHL's all-time leader in Stanley Cups with 11.

Beyond that hardware, Maurice won the Hart Trophy (NHL's MVP) in 1946-47 and finished in the top three in the vote five other times. He finished his 18-year career with 966 points, while Henri got to 1,046 points in his 20 seasons.

The Actors : Dell Curry, Stephen Curry, Seth Curry

The Accolades : 12 All-Star Selections, 2 MVPs, 2 scoring titles, 4 NBA Championships, 214.0 win shares

Hands down, this was the toughest ranking on this list.

Pitch the premise of "Ranking the Best Sports Families" to anyone in sports media over the past decade. The Curry family will likely be one of the first that springs to mind.

Steph is doing all of the heavy lifting here. He accounted for more than two-thirds of the 214.0 win shares and every other accolade listed above, as the NBA's all-time leader in made three-pointers (by a laughable margin).

When Dell's career ended, his biggest claim to fame was either winning Sixth Man of the Year in 1993-94 or being drafted twice by Major League Baseball before fully committing to basketball. Seth has been "Steph's little brother" for his entire career.

The youngest Curry has played 12 years in the NBA, while the patriarch of this family had a 16-year career. Add that to Steph heading into his 18th season, and you have one family spanning nearly a half-century on an NBA roster.

The Curry trio enters the 2026-27 season with a combined total of 44,745 career points. If nothing else, that's slightly more than the 43,624 points LeBron and Bronny James have combined.

The Actors : Gordie Howe, Mark Howe, Marty Howe

The Accolades : 2 Hall of Famers, 27 All-Star Selections, 4 Stanley Cups, 6 Hart Trophies, 6 Ross Trophies, 338.6 point shares

Gordie Howe also had a brother, Vic, who played 33 NHL games, but "Mr. Hockey" and his two sons are the ones most hockey fans know.

Before anyone knew about the next generation of Howes, Gordie was already the greatest hockey player of all time. Mario Lemieux and Wayne Gretzky have since surpassed him, but he's still a Mount Rushmore skater with an astounding 2,358 career points across his 26 NHL and six WHA seasons.

Gordie, Mark and Marty played together for seven seasons, with dad coming out of retirement to join his boys with the WHA's Houston Aeros. They combined for 449 goals and 747 assists in their six years in the WHA. That also includes another 122 points when they all went to the NHL for the 1979-80 season.

While that was pretty much the end of the road for both Gordie and Marty, Mark was just getting started on his Hall of Fame journey.

Mark was a left wing during his six years in the WHA, but he spent most of his NHL career as a defenseman. He was named an All-Star in 1981, 1983, 1986 and 1988. He ranks 12th all-time in NHL plus/minus and fifth in WHA history.

The Actors : Bruce Matthews, Clay Matthews Jr., Clay Matthews III, Jake Matthews

The Accolades : 1 Hall of Famer, 25 Pro Bowls, 1 Super Bowl, 548 Approximate Value

The Matthews family tree actually runs deeper than this.

Patriarch Clay Sr. played four seasons in the 1950s, while Clay III's generation includes one brother (Casey Matthews) and three cousins (Kevin Matthews, Mike Matthews, and Troy Niklas) who at least made NFL rosters.

Even if we disregard those five non-Pro Bowl members of this family, though, the overall Matthews footprint in the NFL is staggering.

Bruce was one of the greatest offensive linemen ever. Only Tom Brady (15) has amassed more Pro Bowl selections than Bruce's 14. Only 12 players have a greater career approximate value than Bruce's 214.

Despite that, he makes up only 39 percent of the AV here. Clay Jr. (139), Jake (100 and counting) and Clay III (95) each carved out impressive careers of their own.

All four were first-round draft picks, with Jake going highest at No. 6 overall.

Clay Jr. and Clay III combined for 174 career sacks and more than 2,000 tackles. Both arguably belong in the Hall of Fame alongside Bruce.

The Actors : Bobby Hull, Brett Hull, Dennis Hull

The Accolades : 2 Hall of Famers, 3 Stanley Cups, 3 Hart Trophies, 25 All-Star Seasons, 346.7 point shares

Imagine racking up more than 300 goals and 300 assists in your 14-year NHL career, only to be the oft-forgotten third member of your family's legacy.

Such is life for Dennis Hull, who played in five All-Star Games, accounted for an impressive 67 points in his postseason career and still couldn't hold a candle to his brother or his nephew.

Dennis' brother, Bobby, was one of the all-time hockey greats. Between his 16 seasons in the NHL and seven years in the WHA, he scored 913 goals and a grand total of 1,808 points. Even though the WHA years don't count toward his standing for NHL records, he's still top-30 all-time in points. He would rank comfortably in the top 10 if those seven years in Winnipeg were included.

The Golden Jet's son, the Golden Brett, became an all-timer in his own right. He ultimately joined his father in the Hall of Fame.

Brett's 741 regular-season goals rank fifth on the NHL's all-time leaderboard. He's also fourth on the career postseason goals leaderboard with 103. He is the all-time postseason leader in both power-play goals (38) and game-winning goals (24). He's tied with some guy named Wayne Gretzky in the latter department.

All told, including Bobby's WHA stats and their postseason totals, the trio tallied 2,198 goals and 2,121 assists.

The Accolades : First and only three-time undisputed heavyweight champion of the world (Muhammad), WBC/WIBA World Super Middleweight champion (Laila), combined record of 80-5 with 58 wins by knockout

Even if you've never watched a boxing match, you're surely familiar with Muhammad Ali's work.

Regarded by many (and especially by himself) as the greatest boxer of all time, Ali was also maybe the most polarizing sports figure ever to walk the earth. His battles with Joe Frazier were legendary, while his religious conversion/name change and refusal to serve in Vietnam were highly controversial.

He floated like a butterfly. He stung like a bee. He also had a daughter who became one of the greatest female boxers ever.

Laila's demeanor in the ring and in the media couldn't have been more different from her father's, but she was just as dominant. She went a perfect 24-0 in her career and was crowned world champion in two different divisions.

For one family to produce a top-five male boxer of all time and a top-five female boxer of all time is absurd. That'd be like if Jack Nicklaus were Annika Sörenstam's father, or if Billie Jean King were Rafael Nadal's mother.

The Actors : Ralph Earnhardt, Dale Earnhardt Sr., Dale Earnhardt Jr.

The Accolades : 1956 NASCAR Sportsman Champion (Ralph), seven-time Winston Cup Series Champion (Sr.), two-time NASCAR Busch Series champion (Jr.), three-time Daytona 500 Winners, more than 100 combined wins in NASCAR Cup Series

To celebrate NASCAR's 75th anniversary in 2023, a voting panel named the 75 greatest NASCAR drivers of all time.

Several families are represented twice on that list, including Bill and Chase Elliott, Kurt and Kyle Busch and Bobby and Terry Labonte. Fittingly, though, the Earnhardt family is the only one with three representatives.

Ralph was the patriarch who first infused the bloodline with a love for auto racing, dominating every short track close to his North Carolina home over the course of more than two decades. For all his success, Dale Sr. became an icon.

The Intimidator's No. 3 was quite possibly tattooed on more bodies than any other number in sports history. He won 76 Winston Cup races in his career and is the only driver in NASCAR history to win in four different decades.

Dale Jr. made quite the name for himself, too, as fans voted him NASCAR's most popular driver every year from 2003-17. His 26 wins between the Winston Cup and Chase eras pale in comparison to his dad's 76, but both Earnhardts rank comfortably in the top 50 all time.

The Accolades : 7 MVPs, 17 All-Star Selections, 12 Silver Sluggers, 11 Gold Gloves, 1,094 combined home runs, 974 combined stolen bases, 220.7 bWAR

José Ramírez will almost certainly join this exclusive club before he retires, but for now, there are only three players in MLB history with at least 330 home runs and at least 330 stolen bases: Bobby Bonds (332 and 461), Barry Bonds (762 and 514) and Barry's godfather, Willie Mays (660 and 339).

There are also only two players in MLB history who have at least five individual seasons with at least 30 home runs and 30 stolen bases: Barry and Bobby.

Say what you will about Barry's legacy as it pertains to the steroid allegations, but it's laughable that the Baseball Hall of Fame wants to pretend nobody named Bonds deserves a plaque.

Bobby's candidacy is debatable. His raw career numbers are remarkable, but he was only a three-time All-Star who never won an MVP award or a World Series.

Barry was a seven-time MVP and is MLB's all-time leader in home runs, walks and wins above replacement. Good luck trying to tell the story of Major League Baseball from 1990-2007 without him.

The Actors : Serena Williams, Venus Williams

The Accolades : 30 Grand Slam singles titles, 14 Grand Slam doubles titles (together), 4 Grand Slam mixed doubles titles (two each), 3 Olympic Gold medals in doubles, 2 Olympic Gold medals in singles, nine head-to-head battles in major finals

Wimbledon is arguably one of the 10 most iconic sports venues in the world. For nearly 20 years, Serena and Venus Williams made Centre Court at Wimbledon their personal playground.

They teamed up to win doubles titles at Wimbledon in 2000, 2002, 2008, 2009, 2012 and 2016. (Serena also won a mixed doubles title at Wimbledon during the absurd 1998 run in which each sister won two mixed doubles titles.)

On the singles front at Wimbledon, Venus won in 2000, 2001, 2005, 2007 and 2008 while Serena won in 2002, 2003, 2009, 2010, 2012, 2015 and 2016. That's a combined 12 single titles in 17 years.

When the Summer Olympics were in London in 2012, of course they dominated. The sisters won doubles gold the day after Serena won singles gold.

Even if you ignore all they accomplished at Wimbledon and focus just on the other three Grand Slam events, the Williams sisters would still probably rank in the top 10 here. They've each accomplished so much in their careers spanning more than three decades. Both rank in the top four in career earnings on the WTA Tour.

The Actors : Archie Manning, Peyton Manning, Eli Manning

The Accolades : 1 Hall of Famer, 20 Pro Bowls, 5 MVPs, 4 Super Bowls, 534 Approximate Value

What's wild about the Mannings being an indisputable top-three choice is that they have one of the biggest "What If?" cases in football history in Cooper Manning (spinal stenosis). They also have another generation of quarterbacks on the way, with Arch Manning being the potential top overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Let's ignore those hypotheticals and focus on the three who actually made it.

Dad Archie threw for 23,911 yards and 125 touchdowns in his 13-year career. He's barely in the top 100 in career passing yards now, but when he retired in 1984, he ranked in the top 25 in NFL history.

Those are laughable figures compared to what his sons accomplished, though.

With 57,023 passing yards and 366 passing touchdowns, Eli ranks 11th on both all-time leaderboards, while Peyton's 71,940 yards and 539 touchdowns rank third on both lists.

Those are just the regular-season numbers. Factor in Eli's 2,815 yards and 18 touchdowns and Peyton's 7,339 yards and 40 touchdowns in the postseason, the Mannings have accounted for more than 92 miles' worth of passing yards and more than 6,500 points.

Eli and Peyton went 5-2 combined in the postseason against Tom Brady, who could have won as many as 12 Super Bowls if not for the Manning Bros.

articles.title: NHL Preseason Roundup: Dan Vladar injury, Semyon Varlamov return and Ivar Stenberg debut headline a busy night across the league
articles.summary: NHL News: Catch up on the latest NHL preseason action featuring Dan Vladar's injury, Semyon Varlamov's impactful return, and Ivar Stenberg's impressive debut for the Sharks. Discover standout performances and game results from across the league as teams gear up for the regular season.
articles.body: There were several notable developments around the league in the latest slate of NHL preseason action. Dan Vladar exited early in the Philadelphia Flyers’ 5-1 loss to the Boston Bruins, and Semyon Varlamov returned for the New York Islanders.Elsewhere, 2026 second-overall pick Ivar Stenberg made his debut for the San Jose Sharks, and Anders Lee scored twice in his first game with the Utah Mammoth. It was a big night for the Detroit Red Wings, Buffalo Sabres and Nashville Predators as well.Dan Vladar injury, Semyon Varlamov return and Ivar Stenberg debut stand out from Tuesday’s action Philadelphia Flyers goaltender Dan Vladar left their 5-1 preseason loss to the Boston Bruins with an upper-body injury at 13:31 of the first period. He had six saves until Aleksei Kolosov came in for him in net.Boston pulled away late as Michael Eyssimont scored twice, and Morgan Geekie, Brian Halonen and Elias Lindholm also scored. Jeremy Swayman made 20 saves for the Bruins.Vladar entered the preseason with a 29-14-7 record, a 2.42 goals-against average and a.906 save percentage in his first season with Philadelphia.Semyon Varlamov made 10 saves, and the New York Islanders rallied for a 4-3 win over the New York Rangers. It was Varlamov's first NHL appearance since Nov. 29, 2024. The 38-year-old goaltender had been out of game action while recovering from double partial knee replacements.Matias Maccelli had two goals and an assist, while Matthew Schaefer had a goal and two assists. The Islanders came back from down three goals to complete the comeback at Madison Square Garden.San Jose Sharks debutant Ivar Stenberg scored in the shootout and registered an assist against the Vegas Golden Knights.The second overall pick in the 2026 NHL Draft had 22:17 of ice time and four shots on goal. Vegas won 2-1 in a shootout. San Jose’s Michael Misa scored, and Alexander Holtz tied it for Vegas. Golden Knights goalie Carter Hart stopped 28 shots.Which other NHL preseason results stood outDetroit Red Wings beat Pittsburgh Penguins 7-4 with Michael Brandsegg-Nygard scoring twice and Anton Johansson with four assists. Buffalo Sabres also had a convincing 5-1 win over Columbus Blue Jackets. Noah Ostlund had two goals and Owen Power contributed three assists.Anders Lee had a pair in his debut, and the Utah Mammoth beat the Los Angeles Kings 6-3. Lee comes to Utah after being the captain for the New York Islanders. Matthew Wood tallied twice in the third period, and Felix Nilsson scored the overtime winner as the Nashville Predators rallied to beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 3-2 in overtime.The Edmonton Oilers edged the Winnipeg Jets 2-1 in overtime, and the Calgary Flames beat the Vancouver Canucks 3-1. The preseason results give the individual players and prospects a chance to show their stuff before the 2026-27 NHL regular season gets underway.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: AFCON 2027 qualifiers: Teams, top players, schedule, format, matches
articles.summary: The 2027 Africa Cup of Nations will be held in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, with 24 qualification spots up for grabs.
articles.body:
The qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations begin on Thursday, with 48 countries competing to earn spots in Africa’s biggest football tournament.

Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda will cohost AFCON 2027, as the competition returns to East Africa for the first time in 51 years.

Divided into 12 groups, the teams will be involved in a six-round qualifying process that runs to March next year.

Here’s everything to know about AFCON 2027:

Which teams are in the AFCON 2027 qualifiers?

The draw for the AFCON 2027 qualifiers took place in Cairo, Egypt, in May.

The 48 teams competing in the qualifiers are as follows:

Group A : Morocco, Gabon, Niger, Lesotho

Group B : Egypt, Angola, Malawi, South Sudan

Group C : Ivory Coast, Ghana, The Gambia, Somalia

Group D : South Africa, Guinea, Kenya, Eritrea

Group E : Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Sierra Leone, Zimbabwe

Group F : Burkina Faso, Benin, Mauritania, Central African Republic

Group G : Cameroon, Comoros, Namibia, Congo

Group H : Tunisia, Uganda, Libya, Botswana

Group I : Algeria, Zambia, Togo, Burundi

Group J : Senegal, Mozambique, Sudan, Ethiopia

Group K : Mali, Cape Verde, Rwanda, Liberia

Group L : Nigeria, Madagascar, Tanzania, Guinea-Bissau

What are the top AFCON 2027 qualifying matches?

Ivory Coast vs Ghana – Thursday, September 24 at 19:00 GMT

Nigeria vs Madagascar – Friday, September 25 at 16:00 GMT

Morocco vs Gabon – Friday, September 25 at 19:00 GMT

Egypt vs Angola – Friday, September 25 at 19:00 GMT

Algeria vs Zambia – Friday, September 25 at 19:00 GMT

Senegal vs Mozambique – Friday, September 25 at 19:00 GMT

South Africa vs Guinea – Saturday, September 26 at 16:00 GMT

What is the schedule for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers?

The six rounds of AFCON 2027 qualifying will be held across these FIFA international windows:

Rounds 1 and 2: September 21-October 6, 2026

How many teams can qualify for the Africa Cup of Nations?

In total, 24 teams qualify for AFCON 2027.

The general rule is that the top two teams in each group will advance to the finals.

However, in groups containing Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania – who have automatically qualified as cohosts – only the highest-ranked team outside the respective host country will go through.

The qualifiers will be played in a home and away format, with each team playing six matches.

The 36th edition of AFCON will be held in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, bringing the tournament back to East Africa after five decades.

The tournament will run from June 19 to July 17, 2027, at 10 venues across the countries.

The stadiums are in the Tanzanian cities of Dar-es-Salaam, Arusha, Zanzibar, the Kenyan capital Nairobi, and Hoima, Kampala and Lira in Uganda.

Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 in the latest AFCON final on January 18, as Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal in a chaotic contest guided them to their second continental title.

But in March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) made the extraordinary move to strip Senegal of their crown and award it to Morocco.

The controversial decision came after a review of an incident at the end of normal time in the final, which saw most of the Senegalese team temporarily leave the field to protest an added-time penalty awarded to Morocco, which was missed after a lengthy delay.

Senegal have appealed against CAF’s decision, and the appeal will be heard by the Court of Arbitration for Sport on October 8.

Salah, Diaz and Lookman: The top players in AFCON 2027 qualifiers

Two-time African Footballer of the Year Mohamed Salah, who now plays club football for Trabzonspor in the Turkish Super Lig, stars in record seven-time African champions Egypt’s squad.

Fans should also watch out for Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz and teen midfield sensation Ayyoub Bouaddi in the Morocco squad, led by new coach Mohamed Ouahbi, as well as Ademola Lookman and Samuel Chukwueze in the Nigerian side.

Elsewhere, Ghana are strengthened by the return of their attacking midfielder Mohammed Kudus, who missed the FIFA World Cup 2026 during a seven-month injury absence, while Senegal’s midfield features several talents such as Ibrahim Mbaye and Iliman Ndiaye.

Will Mane and Hakimi play in the AFCON qualifiers?

Morocco will be without their key player and captain Achraf Hakimi for the opening two matches as he serves a two-match suspension, alongside Ismael Saibari, who is banned for three games, for unsporting behaviour during the shambolic AFCON final in January.

Senegal will be without Sadio Mane, two-time African Footballer of the Year, as the Al-Nassr player sits out the match against Mozambique with what newly-appointed coach Patrick Vieira described as a “physical issue”.

Which other key players will miss the AFCON qualifiers?

Nigeria’s star striker Victor Osimhen will miss the opening qualifiers against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau as he continues his recovery from a muscle problem. One of Africa’s finest forwards, Osimhen picked up the injury while playing for his Turkish club Galatasaray.

Naby Keita is among the several established names excluded from the Guinea squad, while Tunisia’s Hannibal Mejbri and Ivory Coast’s Amad Diallo are both out with injuries.

Gabon will be without former captain and all-time top scorer Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, who quit international duty, saying he felt “humiliated” by his exclusion and subsequent reinstatement after the AFCON in Morocco in January.

Many other players also called time on their international careers this year. This includes Riyad Mahrez, who guided Algeria to the AFCON 2019 title; Edouard Mendy, Senegal’s first-choice goalkeeper during their AFCON 2021 triumph; and Ghana’s Spanish-born forward Inaki Williams.

How to watch and follow AFCON 2027 qualifying matches?

Fans can catch all the action from the AFCON 2027 qualifiers on the following broadcasters or streaming platforms:

North Africa and Middle East: beIN SPORTS

East Africa: Azam TV, TBC Tanzania, KBC Kenya

The complete list of global broadcasters is here .

Al Jazeera Sport will also bring you live coverage of select matches.

articles.title: Pakistan must ‘catch up’ with India in T20 cricket, says coach Hesson
articles.summary: Pakistan could face India in the knockouts of the Asian Games, where the world champions won gold in 2023.
articles.body:
Head coach Mike Hesson has admitted that Pakistan will have some catching up to do if they are to challenge archrivals India at the Asian Games.

India’s men have won back-to-back Twenty20 World Cups and are also defending champions at the Asian Games.

Since Hesson took over in May last year, Pakistan have lost to India three times in the Asia Cup 2025 and once in this year’s T20 World Cup.

“India are the benchmark in terms of white-ball cricket at the moment, and our challenge is to catch up to that,” said Hesson in Karachi before the team’s departure for Japan.

The men’s cricket at the Asian Games in Japan starts on Thursday.

Pakistan and India have never met at the games but are likely to face-off in the semifinals on October 1 in Nagoya.

“We are certainly preparing as best we can, and if we get an opportunity to play [India], we will certainly put them under pressure like we did in the final of the Asia Cup,” Hesson said of last year’s final in Dubai.

Pakistan will first meet the winners of Pool B – comprising Hong Kong, Oman and Malaysia – in the quarterfinal on September 28.

Hesson said Pakistan need to start well.

“There is a lot of cricket to be played between now and being able to play in the semifinal for both sides, so we are not getting too far ahead of ourselves,” Hesson said.

articles.title: Pirates Get Ahead of the Inevitable With Camilo Doval
articles.summary: The first move the Pirates made to try and bolster their bullpen ahead of the trade deadline was acquiring Camilo […]
articles.body:
The first move the Pirates made to try and bolster their bullpen ahead of the trade deadline was acquiring Camilo Doval from the Yankees on Aug. 1 Pittsburgh landed the right-hander in exchange for catching prospect Omar Alfonzo and outfield prospect Luis Cruz.

On Tuesday, Doval's tenure with the Pirates came to an end. In a somewhat surprising move, he was designated for assignment to make room for Kirby Yates — another deadline acquisition — who returned from the injured list.

"It was a tough decision," Kelly said on Tuesday.

Doval made 20 appearances for the Pirates and went 0-1 with a 3.79 ERA. He had high strikeout totals — 23 in 19 innings — but also walked 14 batters. In 64 combined games between the Pirates and Yankees this season, Doval went 3-2 with a 4.30 ERA and one save

Given the way the team's pitching staff is currently constructed with two bullpen games through the final five games of the season, the Pirates preferred the length some other options offer.

"He had some really good games and a couple tough ones," Kelly said of Doval. "He's got some really good stuff. Ultimately, it really just came down to being able to maximize innings especially with some younger guys, too, that have pitched pretty well themselves."

Another factor that played into the decision was that Doval is entering his final arbitration year this year. With a $6.1 million salary this year, the 29-year-old could command $7-8 million — if not more — for 2027. He will become a free agent at the end of next season.

The decision to DFA him means Doval wasn't to be tendered a contract. Instead of waiting until the offseason to make a move, the Pirates decided to act now. Pittsburgh will be looking to add to its improved bullpen this offseason, but will do so looking for a more cost-effective option.

Houston and Birmingham are out. Pawtucket and Colorado Springs are in.

The UFL announced on Wednesday that the teams moved from existing markets will be relocated to Rhode Island and Colorado for 2027.

The spring league reiterated the plan to expand to 10 teams in 2028, with Utah and Oklahoma joining the operation.

"2026 was an incredible year for the UFL, and seeing the response from our fans, players, and partners has made what comes next even more exciting," UFL co-owner Mike Repole said in a press release. "There is a real energy around this league right now, and we're thrilled to bring that energy to four new markets. We said in July that our next step was finding the right markets, venues, and fan bases where we can work with local leaders to build the strongest franchises for today and for the future, and we believe Colorado, Rhode Island, Oklahoma, and Utah represent those qualities. We're thankful to the local leaders and partners who believed in this vision and have helped us get here. We can't wait to see these markets come to life and the best part is that this is just the beginning."

Colorado will host its first game on Sunday, April 11st Weidner Field in Colorado Springs. Rhode Island gets its home slate rolling on Friday, April 2, at Centreville Bank Stadium in Pawtucket.

articles.title: Esteban Ocon says he's a 'free agent' for 2027 and looking at F1 options beyond Haas
articles.summary: Esteban Ocon said Wednesday he is “definitely a free agent” for the 2027 Formula 1 season as an exit from the Haas team appears likely.  Ocon said he's holdi...
articles.body:
BAKU, Azerbaijan (AP) — Esteban Ocon said Wednesday he is "definitely a free agent" for the 2027 Formula 1 season as an exit from the Haas team appears likely.

Ocon said he's holding talks with other teams as he nears the end of his second season with Haas.

"At the moment I'm definitely a free agent for next year," Ocon said ahead of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix . "There are things in discussion that are out of my control, there are certain topics that are out of my control. I will keep pushing until the end of the year and see how it goes."

Asked if he was speaking with other teams, Ocon added: "Of course."

Ocon has been outscored 18-3 by teammate Oliver Bearman this season, with a best finish of ninth at the Monaco Grand Prix. He defended his record Wednesday, saying "my performance hasn't been an issue this year" as Haas dealt with an inconsistent car.

The French driver, who made his race debut in 2016 and took his sole F1 win with Alpine in 2021, has dropped off the starting grid before. He was replaced at Racing Point at the end of 2018 and spent the following year as a Mercedes reserve before joining Alpine in 2020.

Potential replacements for 2027 could include Formula 2 title contender Rafael Câmara or Japanese driver Ryo Hirakawa.

Câmara is part of the junior driver program as Haas' engine supplier Ferrari, just as Haas' other driver Bearman was. Hirakawa is backed by Haas partner Toyota and has driven two practice sessions for the team this season.

Bearman signaled Wednesday he is likely to stay with Haas for 2027.

articles.title: Max Verstappen rules out 2027 Le Mans 24 Hours bid
articles.summary: Despite not directly clashing with Formula 1, Max Verstappen has dismissed the idea of competing in the 2027 Le Mans 24 Hours, while Lando Norris insists he...
articles.body:
Max Verstappen has ruled out competing at the Le Mans 24 Hours in 2027, but the four-time Formula 1 world champion is eyeing the 24-hour races at the Nurburgring and Spa-Francorchamps.

The recently revealed 2027 F1 calendar left the door ajar for F1 drivers to compete in several of the biggest endurance races on the calendar, with the 24-hour races at the Nurburgring Le Mans and Spa all held on off-weekends for F1.

It is understood that the likes of Spa, which is organised by SRO, had even built in some date flexibility to avoid a direct clash with F1 in the hopes of attracting drivers like Verstappen or Lando Norris to take part in the end-of-June event.

The biggest endurance race, the Le Mans 24 Hours, takes place on 12-13 June next year and is sandwiched between the Monaco and Portugal rounds. But given the extensive preparation needed for the French endurance classic, which includes a test day which clashes with Monaco and is supposed to be mandatory for rookies, Verstappen has now punted the idea of a 2027 Le Mans debut into the long grass.

"Nurburgring and Spa, probably. Le Mans, not. That's not on my list for now," Verstappen said on Wednesday in Baku.

Fernando Alonso , a two-time winner of the event with Toyota, had flirted with the idea of joining forces with Verstappen at Le Mans: " I don't think next year that will happen, but maybe in the future. That would be nice. Max [needs to be] a little bit more free on the calendar. There are a lot of races."

Lando Norris completed a test of McLaren's brand-new Hypercar at Portimao.

Reigning world champion Norris is interested in Le Mans outing in the future but insisted it was "not something I've been thinking about". Last week, the Briton completed a test of McLaren's brand-new Hypercar at Portimao.

"The test was nice to go and do something," Norris said. "All my focus is still on F1 and will always be. I'll never sacrifice something in F1 for something else.

"If there's a chance that things can work out, maybe, but I don't know if this is next year, the year after, three years, four years, I have no idea. It's not something I've been thinking about at all, but it's something I would like to do in the future."

Verstappen was more optimistic about his chances to make his Spa 24 Hours debut, with SRO moving the event's official two-day test to 15-16 June which does not clash with an F1 event.

After his car dropped out of the lead of the Nurburgring 24 Hours with mechanical issues, the four-time F1 world champion is also keen to have another go at the Nordschleife.

"I said already after the race on the Nordschleife that I wanted to go back," the Dutchman confirmed. "So, if it allows me to prepare well and it all works out well, [I will do it].

"I know there is no clash, but it still needs to work out in my schedule, and then I'll do it. And Spa is an exciting option to do it."

Additional reporting by Ronald Vording and Ben Vinel

Sept. 23 (UPI) -- Carolina Panthers running back Jonathan Brooks will undergo core muscle surgery and land on injured reserve, a league source told UPI on Wednesday.

Brooks was hurt in the fourth quarter of 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday in Atlanta. The third-year running back totaled 11 touches for 73 yards from scrimmage through two games this season.

He was limited in practice this week due to a groin injury.

Brooks, who is expected to miss at least six weeks of action, played 30% of the offensive snaps in Week 2. Starter Chuba Hubbard was in for 65% of the snaps. Third-string running back A.J. Dillon played just 6% of the offensive snaps and was in for 12% of the special teams snaps.

Hubbard was in for 71% of the offensive snaps in Week 1, compared to Brooks' 19% share. Dillon played for 10% of the snaps in the Panthers' season opener, a 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears.

Hubbard totaled 151 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns through the Panthers' first two games of 2026. Ahmani Marshall and Anthony Tyus III are the Panthers' practice squad running backs.

articles.title: By the Numbers: Cowboys' run game lagging; defense's shows susceptibility to running QBs
articles.summary: Yes, Dak Prescott's numbers were out of this world. But the ground game is stuck and the defense's weaknesses are starting to become obvious.
articles.body:
The numbers on the scoreboard were the most important ones for the Cowboys in their home opener against Washington , but there was plenty to examine with a deeper dive into the afternoon's statistics, too. And while leveling the team's record at 1-1 was satisfying, that closer look shows there's still a long way to go before Cowboys Nation should feel confident about any talk of being among the league's elite.

Dak Prescott 's numbers in his record-setting performance were magnificent any way you slice them, and KaVontae Turpin had a productive day that may be being overlooked by many simply because he hasn't returned one to the end zone in almost two years. But a second straight game with weak rushing numbers is starting to spell out a troubling trend for Javonte Williams as well as the offensive line blocking for him.

The defensive run game needs work, too, with gaudy rushing totals from Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels spotlighting a (thus far) very exploitable weakness in Christian Parker's unit. And while the third-down defense was better in Week 1, the inability to get off the field should have Cowboys Nation concerned.

Here's our weekly look inside some of the numbers that helped tell the story of the Cowboys' latest outing.

The Cowboys' bellcow is off to a rather lumbering start this season after his career-best 2025 campaign. He gained just 30 yards on 12 carries on Sunday, which is less success than he had in an already-disappointing Week 1. Williams's two-game average of 3.0 yards per tote has him ranked outside the top 40 among all ball carriers across the league.

9.9: Average YPC allowed to Jayden Daniels

Daniels gashed the Cowboys for 69 yards- in just one half- before leaving Sunday's game and averaged 9.9 yards every time he left the pocket. That's more than double the per-rush rate Jaxson Dart recorded in Week 1. The Cowboys defense is currently allowing over 6.5 yards to opposing quarterbacks... and Lamar Jackson is up next. Scheme, gap discipline, poor tackling, whatever the issue... this needs fixing ASAP.

40: Offense's average starting field position

KaVontae Turpin looked much like his old self on Sunday, nearly breaking one kick return for a housecall and averaging 30.5 yards on his four total attempts. That helped give the Cowboys offense a big head start on five of their eight possessions. (Recovering a fumble on the Washington 13 obviously boosted that number on a sixth.) According to DLLS Cowboys , the average starting field position was the team's best for a game since the "Watermelon Kick game" versus Atlanta in Week 2 of the 2020 season.

57.1%: Commanders' 3rd-down percentage conversion rate

The Cowboys stopping Washington on just six of their 14 third-down tries showed how effective the Commanders were at moving the ball, even outgaining Dallas by 50-plus yards by game's end. But at least it was an improvement over the Giants' 9-of-11 success rate in the season opener. Dallas currently has the worst third-down defense in the NFL, one of only six teams allowing opponents to convert third downs at a 50% clip or better.

A second straight game with a team rushing total of below 70 yards has Dallas scraping the bottom of the league in the ground game. Their 135 yards through two games (both against mediocre run defenses) has Javonte Williams & Co. ranked 30th out of all teams thus far this season. It could be even tougher sledding in Week 3, when they face the Ravens , who are currently in the top five when it comes to shutting down the run. And then? It's the Texans , Buccaneers , and Packers , all in the top eight through two weeks.

143.7: Dak Prescott's Week 2 passer rating

The number has been officially adjusted down from Sunday's original data by one-tenth of a point , but Prescott's monster passer rating still ranks as the fourth-best in his entire pro career, which now encompasses 148 games (including playoffs). The last time he crossed the 140 threshold? Thanksgiving 2023, also against Washington.

articles.body:
The Denver Broncos entered the win column in Week 2 after beating the Jacksonville Jaguars, 20-13 , at Empower Field at Mile High on Sunday.

The Broncos used a 17-point surge in the second half to fend off the Jaguars, who were looking for their 10th straight win in the regular season dating back to last year.

Bo Nix went 22-of-31 for 288 yards and one touchdown. He had a field day throwing the ball to Jaylen Waddle , who had eight receptions for 138 yards.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

FanDuel TV's Kay Adams pointed out that Nix threw for 9.3 yards per dropback, the highest average for the Broncos since Peyton Manning threw for 9.9 yards against the Arizona Cardinals in 2014.

"That is the Jayden Waddle effect. That is what we expected, why things should be better than they were last year, why last year shouldn't be the floor, and why what we're seeing this year cannot be the ceiling," said Adams.

"That is what Bo Nix can do when he is able to let it rip and throw it downfield a little bit more. I think this was a huge, huge step forward against a good team."

She described Waddle as a "game-changer." The Broncos traded for Waddle in exchange for draft capital, envisioning him as the perfect target for Nix with his dynamic talent. So far, their connection has been impressive.

Waddle bounced back after a subpar debut for Denver, tallying only one reception in their loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1 .

Adams, meanwhile, noted that Nix appears to be someone who "thrives in chaos," making him a "fourth -quarter machine."

Nix, Waddle, and Jonah Coleman will continue to lead the offense against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.
